# Traits

By skill, then by trait. The vocabulary and lists live in `trait-definitions.yaml` and `traits/`; rulings come from the ledger.

## By skill

### Ours

#### core · Building · Implementation — build-a-lever
- `hand-first-recipe`: Do the first unit by hand, then build the tool and show it reproduces the hand result before running it on the rest.
- `minimal-tool`: Build the smallest script that does or proves the job, never a framework.
- `rerun-safe-tool`: Make a work tool safe to rerun on input it has already changed.
- `proposed-artifact-commit`: Keep a work tool or proof artifact in the scratch folder and propose committing it when the work will be rerun or audited.

#### core · Delivery · Release — harness-publish
- `manual-root-only`: Run publishing as a manual, user-run step only in the source workshop, never in an adopted repo.
- `prerequisites-scope`: Confirm the plugin submodule is initialized with its publish script present, reporting a missing prerequisite rather than pretending publication ran.
- `repo-context-check`: Verify the plugin-owned template, installer, updater and doctor use the shared repo-context location and preserve the glossary.
- `authority-separation`: Confirm publication and commit authority separately, treating a no-commit instruction as binding.
- `preflight-gates`: Before publishing, run the catalog check and require a clean tree unless an explicitly authorized dirty-tree mode applies.
- `dry-run`: Run the publish script's check mode to preview the gates, neutrality audit and rsync diff while writing nothing, fixing anything it reports in the source repo rather than the shipped plugin.
- `publish-bump`: Run the publish bump at the level chosen from what changed, with an optional throwaway smoke install and a dirty-tree override only on explicit consent.
- `plugin-repo-review`: Review the separate plugin repository, stage explicit paths, and commit naming the plugin version and source commit only when commit authority was granted, never pushing.
- `submodule-pointer`: Bump and commit the submodule pointer only when authorized, otherwise report the prepared state and proposed update with an update command verified against the consumer's current CLI.
- `failure-table`: Map each publish-script failure line to its cause and fix.
- `never-edit-build-output`: Never hand-edit the shipped plugin's skills or agents, which are build output; edit plugin-owned skills and scripts in the plugin itself.

#### core · Design · Specification — to-spec
- `synthesize-settled`: When the decisions are already settled, synthesize them into a spec without reopening the discussion.
- `spec-template`: Capture the spec in a fixed skeleton: problem, solution, user stories, implementation decisions, testing decisions, out of scope and further notes.
- `spec-criteria-and-questions`: Add success-criteria and open-questions sections to the spec skeleton.
- `none-keeps-heading`: Keep every spec heading, writing None in an empty section so its absence reads as a decision.
- `testing-seam-decision`: Record in the spec which seam the feature is tested at, preferring an existing and the highest useful seam and the fewest seams.
- `no-stale-file-paths`: Keep concrete file paths out of a durable spec, ticket or brief, describing interfaces and behaviour that survive code drift.
- `no-stale-code-snippets`: Keep code snippets out of a durable spec or ticket because they go stale.
- `prototype-snippet`: Inline a prototype snippet in the spec only when it encodes a decision more precisely than prose can.
- `spec-approval-gate`: Keep a spec in draft until explicit authorization names its direction and scope, with any blocking question resolved or moved to out-of-scope first.
- `material-risk-review`: Route an artifact or change with material risk or a broad blast radius through an independent critic review before it is accepted.
- `user-perspective-framing`: Write a spec's problem and solution from the user's perspective.
- `implementation-decisions-scope`: List a spec's implementation decisions across modules, interfaces, clarifications, architecture, schema, contracts and interactions.
- `testing-decisions-contents`: Record a spec's testing decisions as what makes a good test, which modules are tested and the prior-art tests to follow.

#### core · Discovery · Charting — wayfinder
- `decision-map-epic`: Chart a large effort as one map item on the tracker whose children are decision tickets.
- `plan-not-do`: Keep the map to planning: each ticket resolves a decision rather than executing a build slice.
- `dependency-edges`: Encode real blocking edges in the tracker and let the ready frontier drive execution rather than listing order.
- `map-as-index`: Keep resolution detail on each ticket while the map holds only a named pointer and a gist.
- `map-body-sections`: Structure the map body as Destination, Notes, Decisions so far, Not yet specified, and Out of scope.
- `reference-by-name`: Reference tickets by name with identifiers and links so the map reads without opening every item.
- `bounded-decision-ticket`: Make each ticket one bounded question whose answer is a decision.
- `coherence-sized-tickets`: Size decision tickets by decision coherence and dependencies, not an assumed context-window size.
- `label-free-typing`: Express each ticket's kind through the tracker's native item type and a title prefix, creating no labels.
- `ticket-type-set`: A fixed set of ticket kinds: research for facts, prototype for fidelity, grilling for a live interview, and task for prerequisite work that unblocks a decision.
- `claim-before-work`: Choose the requested or a ready unclaimed child and claim it before working on it.
- `destination-first`: Name the destination first, since it fixes the scope and shapes every ticket.
- `question-graduation`: Ticket a question once it is sharp enough to state, even while blocked, and hold not-yet-specifiable work aside until earlier answers make it expressible.
- `record-resolution`: On resolving a ticket, record the answer on it, close it, and add a pointer to the map's decisions so far.
- `out-of-scope-close`: Close an out-of-scope ticket with an explicit exclusion reason rather than a claim of delivery.
- `human-decision-gate`: Stop at a required human decision and prepare concrete options before requesting the final gate.
- `multi-ticket-sessions`: Continue through additional authorized ready tickets with no one-ticket-per-session limit, parallel work needing disjoint ownership.
- `prototype-ticket-asset`: Resolve a prototype ticket by building a rough artifact and linking it from the ticket as an asset.
- `fog-hygiene`: Keep decided, ticketed and out-of-scope items out of the map's section of not-yet-specified questions.
- `low-res-map-load`: When working a map, load only its low-resolution body and open related tickets only on demand.
- `breadth-first-charting`: Chart by questioning breadth-first across the whole space to surface the open decisions and first steps before going deep on any.
- `invalidated-ticket-reconciliation`: Update or delete the other tickets that a recorded decision invalidated.
- `prerequisite-task-human-checklist`: Do prerequisite task work alone where possible, otherwise hand the human a precise checklist.
- `prerequisite-task-result-facts`: Record on a prerequisite task the resulting facts later tickets depend on, such as URLs or where credentials live.

#### core · Discovery · Research — research
- `decision-framing`: State the decision, scope, constraints and material unknowns, and choose sources by what would change the answer.
- `primary-source-preference`: Prefer primary sources such as official docs, source code and specs over secondary write-ups.
- `source-version-dating`: Record the versions and dates of the sources behind changing facts.
- `vendor-claim-testing`: Test vendor claims with independent observation, distinguishing reported experience from proof.
- `source-weighting`: Weight each source by how well its type supports the claim's domain, discounting weak-alone signals and documented red flags.
- `evidence-separation`: Compare alternatives and counterevidence while separating verified fact, inference, uncertainty and conflicts with recorded decisions.
- `disconfirming-red-team`: Surface the strongest case against the conclusion and name what would reverse the recommendation.
- `structured-synthesis`: For a complex question, organize evidence with a claim table and a pattern scan that turns facts into decision-relevant implications.
- `evidence-lenses`: Apply one to three evidence frameworks (maturity, failure modes, source confidence) to weigh what the sources show, not to pick an option.
- `evidence-without-verdict`: Say what the evidence favours and how strongly, and leave the decision to the caller.
- `cited-artifact`: Bind citations to the claims they support in the research output.
- `scaled-report`: Answer at the requested scale, saving a durable report only when requested or useful for an authorized handoff.
- `area-topic-filing`: Without a path from the caller, file the output under one root by the work's area and topic, reusing an existing folder before creating one, two levels at most, and never replacing an earlier run's file without authority to revise it.
- `decision-sufficient-stop`: Stop investigating when remaining uncertainty no longer changes the decision, or when a named access or budget limit is reached.
- `sizeable-delegation`: Delegate only a sizeable, independent part of the investigation.

#### core · Improvement · Codification — authoring-for-agents
- `surface-choice`: Choose the right owner for an instruction — policy file, project document with a pointer, skill, manual alias, conditional reference, or an existing hook or check — and search for an existing owner first.
- `activation-boundary`: Put the activation boundary first — positive cases and the nearest misleading case to skip — and let a description select rather than duplicate the workflow.
- `inline-vs-disclose`: Inline what every branch needs and disclose branch-specific material behind a conditional pointer.
- `outputs-and-authority`: State outputs, material invariants, authority boundaries and stop conditions explicitly.
- `one-effective-instruction`: Prefer one effective instruction over repeated prohibitions or ritual steps, treating wording techniques as hypotheses rather than laws.
- `context-pointers`: Write a pointer that names the material and the condition for reaching it, front-loading the trigger.
- `two-loads`: Weigh always-loaded context cost on the agent against cognitive load on the human.
- `completion-criteria-clarity`: End each step on an observable, checkable done-or-not-done criterion that resists premature completion.
- `precision-and-discretion`: Match prescription to fragility: exact recipes for deterministic operations, judgment for context-dependent choices.
- `single-source-of-truth`: Keep each meaning in one authoritative place so changing it is a one-place edit.
- `environment-as-cache`: Point to authoritative commands and lookups instead of copying volatile facts the agent can find itself.
- `decision-relevance-pruning`: Keep only content that changes the agent's decisions, such as conventions, non-obvious failure modes, required interfaces and invariants.
- `no-op-deletion`: Delete instructions the model already follows by default.
- `unsupported-claim-removal`: Remove unsupported claims and invented thresholds from instructions.
- `skill-packaging`: Keep one canonical directory per workflow with a SKILL.md, adding references only for substantial conditional material and scripts for reusable mechanical work.
- `invocation-mode`: Choose model-invoked or user-invoked activation, setting the disable-model-invocation flag for manual workflows.
- `invocation-sidecar-sync`: Pair the manual-invocation flag with the provider's implicit-invocation policy and regenerate the catalog and sidecars together after metadata edits.
- `compatibility-alias`: Keep a manual or legacy entrypoint as a thin pointer that delegates to the canonical owner, not as an independent workflow others auto-activate.
- `verification`: Inspect the diff for lost contracts, scale fresh-context and pressure trials to behavioural risk, and report unavailable behavioural checks as a limit instead of manufacturing evidence.
- `mechanical-vs-judgement`: Classify each finding as mechanical (a fixed syntactic pattern suiting a deterministic check) or judgement (cross-file consistency suiting a standards doc).
- `extend-existing-docs-first`: Prefer extending existing pointed-to documents before writing new ones.
- `check-pointer-not-restatement`: Once a check enforces a rule, replace the instruction that restated it with a pointer to the check.
- `judgement-lesson-failure-example`: When a recurring lesson needs judgement and cannot be checked, revise the instruction it implicates and add one example of the failure, rather than repeating or emphasising the rule.
- `build-check-over-rule`: Default to building a deterministic check over writing a prose rule for any mechanical finding.
- `co-location`: Keep a concept's definition, rules and caveats under one heading so reading one part brings its neighbours.
- `completion-criteria-demand`: Phrase the criterion to demand thorough work, driving the legwork latent in its wording.
- `one-trigger-per-branch`: Give each trigger branch of a pointer one trigger, collapsing synonyms.
- `pointer-identity-trim`: Cut from a pointer any identity the target's own body already carries.
- `relevance-check`: Check every line still bears on the document's task, pruning stale or irrelevant ones.
- `sharpen-before-inline`: Fix a weakly reached must-have target by sharpening its pointer's wording first, inlining it only if that fails.
- `split-by-invocation`: Split off a model-invoked skill only when a distinct leading word should trigger it or another skill must reach it.
- `fix-at-highest-level`: Try fixes for a repeated mistake in order of architecture, types, lint or CI, tests and finally docs, stopping at the highest level that works.
- `check-error-names-replacement`: Where wrong code can still compile, add a check whose message points at the specific file, type or function to use.
- `ratchet-on-common-patterns`: When a pattern is already widespread, fail only on changes that add more of it.
- `check-proved-on-real-mistake`: Show each new check failing against a mistake that actually occurred.

#### core · Improvement · Codification — harness-evaluate
- `read-first`: Before judging a candidate, read its canonical source, the relevant prior ledger decision and the closest local implementation, keeping reference repositories as read-only evidence.
- `decision-dimensions`: Weigh a candidate on behavioural gain, overlap, dependencies, context cost and maintenance.
- `disposition-choice`: Choose among reject or defer, merge into an existing capability, a separate plugin for a distinct dependency or domain, or shared-template adoption for broadly useful low-cost guidance.
- `recommendation-vs-record`: Treat evaluation as yielding only a recommendation and record a curation event solely under authorization, one per capability in the open round.
- `record-command`: Append a curation decision with the registry record command carrying its kind, subject, reason and evidence.
- `edit-canonical-source`: Make an authorized adoption edit the one canonical source, placing shared policy in the shared files without duplicating it across provider directories.
- `template-adoption-gate`: For template adoption, verify the initialized template tools, run the sync and template-build scripts, and inspect the neutrality and leak results.
- `material-risk-review`: Route an artifact or change with material risk or a broad blast radius through an independent critic review before it is accepted.
- `adopt-after-state-exists`: Record an adopt or adopt-merged event only after the adopted state exists, passing the adaptation as JSON for a merge, then update the skill's record.

#### core · Improvement · Codification — harness-scan
- `resolve-target`: Resolve the named reference harness or path, asking only when it is ambiguous.
- `drift-scan`: Run the drift scan to surface upstream changes since our pin.
- `gap-report`: Run the gap report for capabilities never ruled on, changed upstream since their ruling, or held but never ruled on.
- `material-report`: Report the material drift and useful candidates against existing equivalents.
- `pin-move-catalog-refresh`: When the submodule pointer moves, regenerate the catalog at the new pin and report which skills need analysis, leaving the review itself to the curation route.
- `beads-followup`: Let the gap command print tracker-create lines to review by hand, never auto-running them, and only within filing authority.
- `pin-preserving-fetch`: Fetching upstream refs updates only the local cache and never moves pinned submodule commits, with a no-fetch option to skip the network when offline.
- `reject-valid`: Treat reject or defer as a valid outcome when a candidate adds no durable behavioural value.

#### core · Improvement · Codification — harness-skill-compare
- `scale-to-question`: Scale comparison depth to the question — descriptions and relevant branches for a narrow overlap, every shipped instruction, metadata and script for a full comparison.
- `inspected-vs-executed`: Distinguish inspected code from executed behaviour and never infer invocation frequency from description text.
- `registry-consult`: Consult the registry index, skill records and reference pages for classification and prior decisions.
- `skill-review-file`: For a durable merge, upgrade or rebuild decision, write a dated skill review file that opens with the compared set and that a later ruling cites as evidence.
- `component-inventory`: Cite each behavioural component — step, gate, template, rule, heuristic or red-flag table — with file and line, treating a heading as not a component.
- `presence-matrix`: Tabulate one row per component and one column per skill, marking present, variant or absent, and explain how each varying row is realised and which is stronger.
- `verdict`: Conclude whether the skills substitute or complement, stating what to take, from where, and what to leave, each with a reason.
- `narrow-stays-in-chat`: Keep a narrow comparison in chat with no file, stating its coverage and any unverified behaviour.

#### core · Improvement · Codification — harness-status
- `drift-scan`: Run the drift scan to surface upstream changes since our pin.
- `summary-table`: Summarise the result as a table of repo, added, removed, material-changed and minor.
- `scan-candidates`: Flag the repos with material changes as candidates for a deeper scan.
- `pin-preserving-fetch`: Fetching upstream refs updates only the local cache and never moves pinned submodule commits, with a no-fetch option to skip the network when offline.
- `offline-continue`: On a failed fetch, note it and continue with the remaining repos.
- `concise-output`: Keep status output to the table plus a one-line recommendation, never dumping full diffs.

#### core · Improvement · Codification — migrate-claude-to-codex
- `dry-run-default`: Preview all planned changes by default and write only under an explicit apply flag.
- `skill-symlinking`: Expose canonical skills to the target runtime via relative symlinks without copying, preserving legacy filename casing at the destination.
- `destination-protection`: Never overwrite an existing skill destination even under force, which applies only to generated scaffolds.
- `command-conversion`: Convert source commands into target skill scaffolds, reporting any name collision with an existing skill.
- `agent-conversion`: Convert source agents into conservative target config scaffolds, inferring a sandbox mode and flagging that model identifiers do not carry over.
- `hook-conversion`: Copy hooks and rewrite hook registrations into the target format, flagging that fixtures must validate before enforcement is trusted.
- `config-scaffold`: Write a target runtime config file and a migration-notes document as scaffolds.
- `shared-policy-untouched`: Leave shared policy canonical and rule or execution-policy routing manual, generating no rule files, execution policy or policy-document edits.
- `structural-verify`: Provide a verify command that parses the generated assets and optionally runs discovery, disclosing that structural success proves neither semantic parity nor routing.
- `non-destructive`: Never delete, stage or commit the source assets.
- `test-before-reliance`: Run the migrator's own tests and trial it in a disposable target before relying on changed behavior.

#### core · Intake · Clarification — discovery
- `match-interaction-to-ambiguity`: Match the interaction depth to the ambiguity — return to the task, ask one focused question, or run a structured exploration — rather than over- or under-investigating.
- `scoped-context-read`: Read only the existing code, authoritative docs and constraints needed to distinguish the live choices.
- `reuse-before-new`: Name the closest existing solution before proposing a new one.
- `decision-frame`: Establish the outcome, intended user, success criteria, constraints and exclusions before committing to an approach.
- `answerer-triage`: Sort each open question by who can answer it (this project's code, cited by file and line; outside sources; a run; a routine pick; the owner) and put to the owner only what the others cannot settle.
- `options-with-tradeoffs`: Present materially different options with their tradeoffs when alternatives remain.
- `question-batching`: Batch independent questions whose prerequisites are settled and defer each dependent question until its prerequisites are answered.
- `recommended-answer`: Attach a recommended answer to each question, letting the respondent disagree.
- `yes-accepts-recommendation`: Word each question so that a yes accepts your recommended answer.
- `round-format`: Lay out each round in a fixed question-and-recommendation markdown format, one block per question.
- `answer-before-next-round`: Wait for the respondent's answers to a round before asking the next one.
- `settled-stop`: Recompute the unresolved choices after each answer and stop once the needed ones are settled, deferred or blocked, without exhausting every branch.
- `self-serve-facts`: Look up available facts yourself rather than asking, leaving only the decisions to the live participant.
- `approval-interpretation`: Treat a clear acceptance of a concrete proposal or an explicit delegation of routine choices as usable authority, and silence as not approval.
- `observable-outcomes`: Translate vague goals such as scalable or simple into observable outcomes only when the distinction affects the design.
- `structured-divergence`: Generate only enough distinct options to expose the tradeoff, compare them on value, feasibility, cost and reversibility, test the assumption most likely to reverse the choice first, and keep rejected options with their reasons.
- `exploration-lenses`: Apply ideation lenses such as SCAMPER or Jobs-to-Be-Done selectively to unlock options, never as a mandatory quota or sequence.
- `assumption-audit`: For each candidate direction, list its assumptions as must be true (dealbreakers that kill it if wrong), should be true (important but the approach can adjust) or might be true (secondary), validate the dealbreakers before building, and leave the might-be-true ones until the core is proven.
- `mvp-scope`: Scope the first version of a chosen direction to one user job done well, sized by what can be built and tested in a time box rather than by a feature list, aimed at the riskiest assumption, with a mandatory list of what it is not doing and why, and expect it to feel incomplete to the builder.
- `judgment-frameworks`: Apply one to three comparison frameworks to sharpen a choice rather than to decorate the report.
- `decision-sequences`: Follow a decision sequence matched to the question's domain, handing its fact-finding steps to `research`.
- `visuals-into-spec`: Re-express an approved diagram inside the durable spec as a Mermaid block, or record what a mockup showed and decided, rather than linking disposable scratch files.
- `html-mockup-on-request`: On explicit request only, produce one self-contained offline HTML mockup under the scratch directory for what a diagram cannot carry.
- `sourced-status-record`: Write one file per run with a row per question giving its answer, its source, a confidence for each established fact and a status (established, decided, routine, proposed, open), marking a material choice decided only on the owner's quoted, dated word or a recorded delegation, and check the file with a script.
- `area-topic-filing`: Without a path from the caller, file the output under one root by the work's area and topic, reusing an existing folder before creating one, two levels at most, and never replacing an earlier run's file without authority to revise it.
- `generated-record-index`: Regenerate one index line per record (date, question, outcome) from the files themselves, never by hand.
- `structure-question-visual`: During design, answer a structure, flow, sequence or state question with an inline visual rather than prose, keeping prose for requirements, scope and trade-offs; the visual's form, size and medium come from the show-me skill's rules.

#### core · Intake · Clarification — grilling
- `map-decisions`: Map the material decisions and their prerequisites before questioning.
- `question-batching`: Batch independent questions whose prerequisites are settled and defer each dependent question until its prerequisites are answered.
- `recommended-answer`: Attach a recommended answer to each question, letting the respondent disagree.
- `self-serve-facts`: Look up available facts yourself rather than asking, leaving only the decisions to the live participant.
- `settled-stop`: Recompute the unresolved choices after each answer and stop once the needed ones are settled, deferred or blocked, without exhausting every branch.
- `absent-respondent`: When the needed respondent is absent, prepare a questionnaire for them instead of interviewing the present user about the subject.
- `grill-the-send`: Ask the present user only about the send (who it goes to and what they need back), never about the subject the recipient knows.
- `gap-targeted-questions`: Aim a questionnaire's questions at the gap between what the recipient knows and what the sender needs.
- `interview-not-authority`: Treat conducting an interview or drafting a questionnaire as neither implementation authority nor permission to send it.
- `optional-docs`: When requested, record settled domain terms and qualifying architectural decisions through domain-modeling, not as an automatic by-product of the interview.
- `decision-summary`: Produce the durable decision log in a fixed template — context, a decision table with rationale and implications, open items, a dependency map and a risk register.
- `answer-before-next-round`: Wait for the respondent's answers to a round before asking the next one.
- `yes-accepts-recommendation`: Word each question so that a yes accepts your recommended answer.
- `importance-ordered-questions`: Order a questionnaire's questions most important first.
- `needed-item-coverage`: Finish a questionnaire only when every needed decision or fact is covered by at least one question.
- `single-idea-questions`: Make each question a single idea, never a compound one.

#### core · Intake · Clarification — restate
- `goal-and-problem-restatement`: Say in your own wording what you believe the user is aiming for and which problem they are trying to solve.

#### core · Intake · Clarification — sharpen
- `depth-not-scope-rewrite`: Treat improving a task as making it deeper, and refuse to make it merely larger.
- `diagnose-then-rewrite-prompt`: Answer a fixed set of diagnostic questions first, then rewrite the prompt to ask for exactly what they revealed.
- `expert-gap-question`: Say what a leading practitioner would do here that the request leaves out.
- `rawest-source-question`: Name the least processed material a practitioner would begin from in place of the summarized input.
- `expert-methods-question`: Name the concrete techniques and instruments a practitioner would apply.
- `outside-correctness-signal`: Name something outside both the agent and the user that would show the result is correct.
- `owner-choices-left-open`: Keep decisions that belong to the user unresolved when rewriting their request.

#### core · Intake · Triage — triage
- `attention-buckets`: Present the items needing triage attention as named buckets, oldest first.
- `triage-decision`: Decide and apply each triage outcome within existing authority rather than deferring every call to the owner.
- `established-notes`: Record what each triage pass settled as a note on the item itself, so the next pass can resume from it.
- `triage-resume-notes`: Resume triage from the notes of earlier passes, never re-asking a question already answered.
- `redundancy-check`: Search the codebase by domain concept for an existing implementation and report where you looked before deciding.
- `prior-rejection-check`: Check earlier rejections for one resembling the request and surface any match before deciding.
- `claim-verification`: Verify a reported claim before acting on it, reproducing a bug or recording exactly why it could not be reproduced.
- `agent-ready-gate`: Make a bead agent-executable only when acceptance criteria, current and desired behaviour, and out-of-scope notes all hold.
- `pick-from-summary`: Show the count and a one-line summary of each waiting item and let the maintainer pick which to triage.
- `durable-rejection-reasons`: Reject only for durable reasons of scope, technical constraint or strategy, treating a temporary reason as a deferral.
- `already-built-close`: Close a request that is already implemented by pointing to where it lives, recording no rejection.
- `brief-acceptance-criteria`: Give every brief concrete, independently testable acceptance criteria.
- `read-full-source-issue`: Read the full body, comments and, for a pull request, the diff of any referenced spec, issue or pull request before working from it.
- `ready-for-human-rationale`: When an item is ready for a human rather than an agent, use the same brief structure but record why it cannot be delegated.

#### core · U · Tutoring — teach
- `learning-shape`: Choose one of a single concept explanation, a session walkthrough, or an explicitly requested ongoing course.
- `level-adaptation`: Infer the learner's level from the conversation and adjust from their responses.
- `what-vs-why`: Separate what happened from why it was chosen when explaining.
- `teaching-workspace`: Keep a multi-session course's state (mission, resources, learning records, glossary and lessons) as files in one course workspace.
- `authorized-course-location`: Open a course workspace only for an explicitly requested ongoing course, in an authorized supplied location, creating its files lazily.
- `mission-grounding`: A mission document capturing the concrete real-world reason for learning that anchors every teaching choice.
- `glossary-entry-template`: Write glossary entries of a term and its definition, grouped under subheadings when clusters emerge.
- `canonical-term-and-aliases`: Pick one preferred term per concept and list its other words as aliases to avoid.
- `tight-concept-definitions`: Define each glossary term tightly by what it is, not what it does.
- `glossary-self-vocabulary`: Use the glossary's own terms inside its other definitions.
- `glossary-admission-on-use`: Add a term to the learner's glossary only once the learner can use it correctly.
- `learning-records`: ADR-like records of lessons and established prior knowledge that steer what to teach next.
- `learning-resource-register`: Keep a course resources file that groups sources into knowledge and community sections and annotates each with what it covers and when to use it.
- `high-trust-resource-filter`: Admit only high-trust sources to the resources file, leaving out marketing posing as education.
- `resource-gap-register`: List the areas the learning goal needs but no good resource covers in a gaps section of the resources file.
- `prune-invalid-resources`: Remove resources that proved wrong, shallow or off-mission rather than keeping them.
- `lesson-format`: Make each lesson short and self-contained, teaching one tightly scoped objective tied to the learner's goal.
- `reusable-assets`: Reuse existing lesson assets before creating new ones.
- `quiz-answer-hygiene`: Keep quiz options plausible and free of giveaways, never matched to exact answer length.
- `retrieval-practice`: Have the learner retrieve answers from memory through exercises or questions.
- `scope-discipline`: Record progress only within course scope and never treat the repository root as a teaching workspace.
- `sourced-explanations`: Draw explanations from trusted, cited sources and check unfamiliar or changing facts rather than relying on unverified recall.
- `mission-interview-first`: When the learning mission is unclear or empty, ask the learner why they want to learn before teaching.
- `community-opt-out`: Respect the learner's choice not to join communities and record it.
- `learning-record-criteria`: Write a learning record only for demonstrated understanding, disclosed prior knowledge, a corrected misconception or a mission shift, never for coverage, glossary duplicates or activity logs.
- `field-term-resolution`: Record in the glossary how loosely used field terms are resolved in this workspace.
- `in-place-definition-revision`: Revise glossary definitions in place as understanding deepens.
- `mission-document-template`: Write the learning mission as why, success criteria, constraints and out of scope.
- `one-mission-per-workspace`: Keep exactly one mission per learning workspace.
- `one-screen-mission`: Keep the mission document within one screen.
- `minimal-learning-record-template`: Write a learning record as a title and one to three sentences of what was learned and why it matters later.
- `learning-record-supersession`: Mark a contradicted learning record superseded rather than deleting it.
- `cross-linked-lessons`: Cross-link lessons to other lessons and reference documents.
- `domain-vocabulary`: Use the project's established domain vocabulary throughout what you write.
- `sequential-record-numbering`: Number a new record one above the highest existing number in its folder.
- `optional-record-sections`: Add optional sections to a record, such as status or consequences, only when they carry real information.
- `knowledge-skills-wisdom-frame`: Frame learning as knowledge from trusted sources, skills from interactive lessons and wisdom from communities.
- `mission-shift-handling`: When the mission shifts or goes stale, confirm with the learner, revise the mission and add a learning record.
- `spacing`: Space practice over time to build long-term retention.
- `storage-strength`: Favour long-term retention over in-the-moment fluency, which can give an illusory sense of mastery.
- `vary-answer-position`: Vary which position holds the correct answer across questions so order gives nothing away.
- `what-how-why-account`: Cover what a thing is, how it operates and why it has that design.
- `single-blended-account`: Merge the findings of separate investigations into one continuous explanation, never separate reports.
- `lead-with-what-matters`: Open an explanation on its central point and on what matters most to this reader.
- `confidence-language-kept`: Keep the tier words and hedges that mark uncertainty when editing a finished answer.
- `pick-few-takeaways`: Choose a small number of things the person should come away understanding before explaining anything.
- `learner-context-from-conversation`: Work out why the person is asking and what they already know from the conversation, not by questioning them.
- `depth-where-asked`: Omit what the person evidently already knows and spend the depth on the area they asked about.
- `orient-then-use-investigation`: Read a body of work only far enough to get oriented, and take the digging from a dedicated investigation rather than redoing it.
- `plain-definition-first`: Begin by naming the thing and defining it in general terms, using its common name if one exists.
- `general-tied-to-local-case`: After the general definition, connect it to how this codebase uses the idea.
- `build-up-order`: Proceed from definition to mechanism, then deeper reasons, then edge cases.
- `problem-and-mechanism-per-part`: For each part, explain the problem it addresses and how it actually operates.
- `walkthrough-of-user-action`: When it helps the idea land, trace what happens step by step as someone performs the action.
- `no-symbol-inventory`: Do not substitute a list of functions and constants for an explanation.
- `no-labels-or-step-words`: Print no stock labels announcing the key idea, and never echo a skill's step wording as headers or phrases.
- `requested-depth-first-answer`: In conversation, give a short complete answer first and stop, and give a requested walkthrough, lesson or full account whole in one reply.
- `offer-depth-follow-lead`: Invite the person to go deeper or change topic, and let them steer.
- `no-teaching-theatre`: Do not announce pauses, sentences to master, or that a part is hard or important; state it, and actually stop when a pause is wanted.
- `show-the-real-artifact`: Bring up the actual diff, source or debugger when that conveys the point most quickly.
- `figure-when-faster`: Add a figure when a picture would land faster than prose, and omit one for a single simple point.
- `incremental-diagram-series`: For three or more moving parts, draw a sequence in which each figure repeats the last and adds exactly one part, and never rely on one complete figure, of whatever kind.
- `plain-colleague-voice`: Write in plain spoken English as if to a coworker, removing filler and hedging while keeping the piece that makes the idea click.
- `reply-is-the-deliverable`: Return the deliverable itself as the reply, never an account of what was done to produce it.
- `threads-to-chase`: Include the lines of inquiry worth pursuing further.

#### core · Verification · Review — interrogate
- `break-it-mandate`: Assign adversaries to try to break a change or design rather than assess it in general.
- `run-proven-finding`: Let a finding stand only when a run executed in the review shows it, so a claim nobody ran is no finding.
- `named-scope-first`: Use the scope the user names when one is given.
- `intent-restated-first`: Restate the change's intent in your own words before sending out adversaries.
- `intent-from-stated-sources`: Take a change's intent only from a stated source such as the request, a brief, a spec or a bead, never from the diff.
- `ask-or-not-run-on-intent`: Ask when the intent is unclear and someone can answer, and report the review as not run when nobody can.
- `own-output-location`: Give every candidate or adversary a separate output location, so they share no writable state.
- `dropout-proceeds-noted`: Go on with the remaining candidates or adversaries when one produces nothing, and record the dropout.
- `verified-snapshot-copy`: Give each adversary and each replay a disposable copy made from one pristine snapshot of the working state and checked against it, reporting not run when a copy cannot be made exact.
- `adversaries-by-model-or-angle`: Run one adversary per available model on one instruction to break the work or, with a single model, several whose prompts each attack something different, giving every adversary the scope and the intent.
- `run-against-real-code`: Require each finding to be demonstrated by executing something against the actual code, such as a failing test, a reproduction script or revealing command output.
- `design-proof-by-probe`: For a design or plan, prove a finding by running a prototype or probing the current tree.
- `repros-stay-in-copy`: Keep each adversary's reproduction material inside its own output location.
- `finding-repro-report`: Require each finding to carry a title, the exact command, the printed output and the output the intent requires.
- `no-findings-valid`: Accept a report with no findings as a valid result, and say so explicitly when none remain.
- `coordinator-replays-finding`: Have the coordinator verify each finding by running its command again.
- `reproduced-and-breaks-intent`: Keep a finding only if the output shows the failure and that failure breaks the stated intent.
- `three-replay-outcomes`: Sort each replayed finding into reproduced, not reproduced (dropped and stated as unreproduced, not disproved) or unreplayable (listed with no severity).
- `merge-by-root-cause`: Combine findings that share one root cause.
- `union-of-verified-findings`: Keep every verified finding across adversaries rather than selecting one adversary's list.
- `output-opens-with-intent`: Open the output with the intent restatement.
- `output-finding-fields`: For each verified finding, report its command, its output and how it breaks the intent.
- `adversary-attribution`: Name the adversaries that found each verified finding.
- `dropped-finding-accounting`: Report for each adversary how many findings were dropped and why.
- `checkout-change-check`: After each adversary returns, compare the shared checkout with the snapshot's state and report each changed path, without voiding the run, restoring anything or naming who changed it.
- `unresolved-outranks-verdict`: Give no favourable verdict while an observed failure stays unreproduced or unreplayable.
- `no-self-adversary`: Report not run rather than attack as an adversary work you wrote or a design you settled.

#### core · Verification · Review — no-comments
- `merge-base-through-tree-scope`: When no scope is named, review the branch from where it left the base branch up to and including the working tree.
- `named-scope-first`: Use the scope the user names when one is given.
- `comment-pass-stays-in-bounds`: During a comment pass, change only comments, and only inside the given scope.
- `kept-code-not-guilty`: Refuse flags that treat intentionally retained code as being at fault.
- `reshape-flags-open-apart-from-comment`: Keep flags asking to restructure surprising first-party code open, whether their comments stay, go or come back.
- `suppressions-in-comment-sweep`: Include lint and type-checker suppression comments in a comment sweep.
- `thin-importance-comment-check`: Before accepting a thinly justified decision on a comment marked important, investigate its symbol's behaviour and history.
- `trivial-flag-direct-fix`: Resolve simple accepted flags at once through edits such as removing an unused path or parameter, or calling the genuine interface.
- `named-workarounds-removed`: Eliminate every workaround the findings name.
- `cheapest-enforcement-offer`: For other constraint comments, propose the least costly enforcement available in scope, whether a type, runtime check, test or CI lint.
- `encoding-approval-gate`: Apply an encoding only with approval, through the route the caller names or given by the caller in advance.
- `encode-then-delete`: When an encoding is approved, add the enforcement and then remove the comment.
- `unencoded-constraint-kept-and-reported`: Without an approved enforcement, keep a constraint comment, report the constraint as open and sketch any out-of-scope work.
- `comment-sweep-report`: Report the comments deleted, those restored on proof, those kept and flagged, the fixes, the enforcements offered and done, the constraints left unenforced and the open items.

#### core · Verification · Review — review
- `independent-critic-verdict`: A reviewer who did not author the work gives evidence-backed findings and a verdict, approving only what was verified and listing the rest as unverified.
- `severity-and-verdict`: Rate each finding by consequence and approve only with no open blocker or major, otherwise require revision, never counting preference alone as a finding.
- `scope-establishment`: Fix the diff and the base it is measured from before reviewing.
- `pre-existing-edit-separation`: Separate pre-existing edits from the task's own changes using the task baseline, not filenames.
- `callers-and-evidence`: Read enough surrounding code and affected callers, treating implementer and reviewer reports as evidence to verify rather than authority.
- `mechanical-gate-precedence`: A failing mechanical verification gate returns the work unreviewed as failed verification unless the requester explicitly waives it.
- `requirements-before-quality`: Check missing, extra and misunderstood requirements before judging code quality.
- `distinct-axis-verdicts`: Report each review axis's verdict separately so one axis passing never masks another failing.
- `test-quality-judgment`: Judge tests by whether they detect meaningful failures with independent expectations, and do not treat test changes as inherently defects.
- `actionable-defects-only`: Report only actionable defects with trigger, consequence and evidence, defer formatting to configured tools, and state plainly when none are found rather than inventing findings.
- `read-only-isolation`: A read-only review preserves the checkout, index and refs, using permitted isolated facilities for any check that needs mutation.
- `verdict-contract`: Dispatched reviewers and re-reviews emit a fixed verdict output of verdict, unverified requirements, located issues and actual checks with limitations.
- `re-review-finding-tracking`: A re-review rules each prior finding addressed or not with located evidence, flags new breakage in the fix delta, and may rule a finding incorrect without demanding cosmetic edits.
- `document-review`: Check a spec or plan against repository context for internal inconsistency, missing constraints, unverifiable claims and scope bloat, editing only unambiguous wording when fixes were requested.
- `finding-adjudication`: Verify each incoming review finding against requirements, code and primary evidence before acting, and give each a visible disposition: fix a confirmed in-scope defect, answer an incorrect one with a retained ruling, record an out-of-scope follow-up.
- `fixed-point-preflight`: Confirm the review ref resolves and the diff is non-empty before fanning out, failing fast rather than inside sub-agents.
- `spec-source-discovery`: Find the originating spec in a fixed order — commit issue references, a user-supplied path, conventional spec directories — and ask only as a last resort.
- `missing-spec-axis-skip`: When the user confirms no spec exists, skip the spec review axis and report that no spec was available.
- `two-axis-review`: Review a diff along two separate axes — conformance to the repo's documented standards and faithfulness to the originating spec.
- `standards-source-discovery`: Search the repo for every file documenting how code should be written, always including the conventional standards and contributing files.
- `cited-standard-findings`: Cite the standard's file and rule for every violation and quote the hunk for every smell.
- `spec-conformance-findings`: Report spec findings as missing or partial requirements, unrequested behaviour and wrongly implemented requirements, quoting the spec line for each.
- `breakage-beyond-callers`: Spend the effort on breakage text search cannot reveal, not on listing callers.
- `safety-fact-proved-by-run`: Treat a convincing writeup as worthless by itself, and prove the fact a change's safety rests on by running real code and including what happened.
- `evidence-ladder`: Grade each safety-bearing fact as asserted, cited to a line, failure walked through, executed in a script or test, or reproduced in the running product.
- `ladder-as-far-as-cheap`: Take each fact as far up the evidence ladder as is cheap and state where it stopped.
- `small-real-library-script`: Normally reach the executed level with one short script that imports the library shipped with the product and calls exactly the function at issue.
- `failing-loud-proof`: Make a proof script or test fail noisily if the claim is wrong.
- `whole-change-including-unstated`: Go through the diff, the symbols added, changed and deleted, and the behaviour change the diff does not spell out.
- `change-history-pull`: Retrieve the related pull request and commits while reading a change.
- `single-safety-fact-search`: Find the one fact that makes a change safe and clears most risky cases, and spend the time there, not on a long list of possibilities.
- `dependency-source-and-pin`: Read the called library's source and confirm its pinned version and whether it is locally patched.
- `timing-and-lifecycle-analysis`: Work out when things execute, including deferred callbacks, teardown and framework differences.
- `non-symbol-coupling-trace`: Follow links symbol search misses: returned data shapes, database columns, wire formats, another language reading the same bytes, feature flags and code several hops away.
- `likelihood-and-cost-per-risk`: Give each risk an honest probability and an honest cost.
- `confirmed-and-cleared-split`: Keep confirmed risks apart from those checked and cleared, saying why each cleared one is fine.
- `empty-search-is-finding`: Count a search that returned nothing as a result to report, not as work to discard.
- `handback-what-it-does`: Say what changed, including the non-obvious part.
- `handback-safety-fact-with-grade`: State the safety fact, its ladder level and its proof, or mark it unproven.
- `handback-risk-fields`: For each risk give how it breaks, the actual file and line, likelihood and severity, how to check it, and the proof for those that matter.
- `handback-pre-merge-check`: Give the cheapest test or reproduction able to expose the actual bug, along with any script written.

#### core · X · Communication — brief-me
- `next-action-first`: Lead with the next concrete action — a command, path or snippet — before any prose.
- `numbered-steps`: Render multi-step work as a numbered list with one bounded action per step.
- `single-next-action`: Close with exactly one concrete next action the reader can do in under two minutes.
- `tangent-suppression`: Finish the current issue first, then offer any other concern as a separate question.
- `state-restatement`: Restate the current progress state every turn so the reader need not hold it in memory.
- `concrete-time-estimates`: Give estimates in concrete units as agent execution plus review time rather than human workdays.
- `visible-progress`: Show completed work in concrete, runnable terms instead of burying it in a recap.
- `matter-of-fact-errors`: State an error's cause and fix plainly with no alarm language.
- `capped-lists`: Cap a list at five items, ranking them or splitting into now and later.
- `no-preamble`: Open with the answer and stop when it is done, with no preamble, recap or closing pleasantry.
- `explain-on-request`: When the user asks to explain or walk through, run as long as the topic needs while keeping the brevity discipline.
- `debug-spiral-reset`: After repeated failed fix turns, stop iterating on code, name the assumption that may be wrong, and ask one diagnostic question.
- `repitch-trigger`: When a message did not land, stop and re-pitch it rather than adding more.
- `controlled-language`: Re-pitch in controlled simplified language with short sentences and common words.
- `domain-vocabulary`: Use the project's established domain vocabulary throughout what you write.
- `pre-send-check`: Before sending, delete announcements, closers, sidebars and empty hedges.
- `repitch-explains-project-terms`: Drop technical jargon from a re-pitch, keeping a project term only with a plain explanation of it.

#### core · X · Communication — html-artifact
- `self-contained-contract`: Produce one HTML file with inline CSS and JS, viewport metadata and no build step, working offline with no external fonts, trackers, fetches or runtime assets.
- `accessibility-contract`: Use semantic markup, keyboard access and adequate contrast, adapt to narrow screens, honour reduced motion, and provide print styles.
- `progressive-enhancement`: Ensure the explanation, data and limitations exist before scripts run and survive with JavaScript disabled.
- `honest-content`: Show only sourced data and explicitly label assumptions and illustrative values.
- `preset-report`: Shape a skim-by-section report — orientation KPIs, numbered sections with a per-type order, and a source footer.
- `preset-dashboard`: Shape a chart-first document where prose only captions inline-SVG charts, with a drill-down data table.
- `preset-explainer`: Shape a concept walkthrough — a TL;DR box, question-headed sections, a glossary and tabbed samples.
- `preset-editor`: Shape an interactive throwaway editor built around a mandatory paste-ready export, with no backend or persisted storage.
- `tokens-first-style`: Derive the artifact's styling from the project's own tokens when they exist, otherwise apply the default neutral aesthetic, never inventing look-alike tokens.
- `component-vocabulary`: Lay content out from a small set of components — KPI tiles, numbered section headers, copy-button code blocks, severity tags, native collapsibles and inline SVG — shaped to the content rather than translating markdown one-to-one.
- `svg-figure-grammar`: Draw inline SVG figures with a viewBox for scaling, currentColor ink, orthogonal masked connectors, a defined paint order and a bottom legend, keeping real text and rounded coordinates.
- `svg-complexity-budget`: Hold each figure to at most nine nodes, twelve arrows and two accents, splitting into overview-plus-detail rather than shrinking, and omit a figure a sentence can carry.
- `svg-accessibility`: Give each inline SVG a role, figure-prefixed title and description IDs, carry meaning in both shape and colour, and mark direction on every edge.
- `honest-data-encoding`: Never clip, truncate, impute or move a mark to make a chart legible; disclose the domain drawn and name any exemption.
- `deliver-verify`: Deliver a link rather than pasted source and verify content fidelity, local links, key interactions, responsive and print behaviour and JS-disabled readability, reporting checks that could not run.

#### core · X · Communication — show-me
- `minimal-visual-selection`: Use the fewest and smallest visuals that make the point, never a gallery.
- `visual-form-catalog`: Offer a set of inline visual forms — pseudocode, call, component and file trees, Mermaid and whole-block — each with its own shape rules.
- `structural-diff`: Show a change as a diff against the structure the reader already holds rather than against raw source.
- `visual-placement`: Place each visual immediately after the sentence it supports and include only the detail the current question needs.
- `real-code-names`: Use real names from the actual code, never invented placeholders.
- `medium-appropriate-form`: Prefer text forms over Mermaid in a terminal and a table over any diagram for a flat list or comparison.
- `html-handoff`: Escalate to the dedicated HTML-artifact skill only under its full gate, and never emit rendered HTML directly.

#### core · X · Communication — unslop
- `meaning-preserved-edit`: Change wording only, never facts, citations or code.
- `confidence-language-kept`: Keep the tier words and hedges that mark uncertainty when editing a finished answer.
- `ing-phrase-cut`: Delete tacked-on present-participle phrases that claim significance, or back them with real sources.
- `vague-attribution-cut`: Name the source of any claim credited to unnamed groups, or delete the claim.
- `name-the-mechanism`: Rewrite a sentence that conveys an impression so that it states a mechanism or number, cutting it if it cannot become an instruction, fact or figure.
- `filler-phrase-cut`: Shorten wordy stock phrases and delete empty announcements of importance.
- `chatbot-phrase-cut`: Remove assistant pleasantries, offers of further help and excited discovery lines.
- `sycophancy-cut`: Remove praise and agreement openers and answer directly.
- `generic-conclusion-cut`: Replace optimistic sign-offs with specific plans or facts.
- `tell-vocabulary-swap`: Replace a fixed list of overused elevated words with plain ones.
- `plain-is-has`: Use is or has in place of grand verbs standing in for them.
- `plain-word`: Use the common word over a fancier synonym.
- `synonym-cycling-cut`: Keep one term for one referent instead of rotating through synonyms.
- `local-metaphor-noun-swap`: Replace figurative pseudo-technical nouns with concrete words, keeping those that name real things in this repository.
- `not-just-but-cut`: Replace the construction that denies one thing to promote another with a direct statement of the point.
- `forced-triplet-cut`: List as many items as naturally exist, never forcing a group of three.
- `false-range-cut`: Replace a from-to construction that has no real scale with a direct list.
- `hedge-stack-trim`: Reduce piled-up qualifiers to a single modal.
- `dense-sentence-split`: Split or trim any sentence the reader must reread to parse.
- `active-voice`: Name the actor in place of a passive, keeping passive only when the actor is unknown or does not matter.
- `adverb-cut`: Cut an adverb, using a stronger verb or the measured figure in its place.
- `mannered-prose-cut`: Replace aphorisms, rhetorical fragments, personified code, figurative verbs and stock framing with literal phrasing.
- `over-compression-fix`: Restore articles, verbs and whole sentences, and spell out arrows, symbols and abbreviations.
- `no-em-dash`: Use no em dashes, ending the sentence or using a comma or parentheses to separate a thought.
- `mid-sentence-colon-cut`: Keep colons for lists and examples, rewriting mid-sentence uses and the comparison framing around them.
- `bold-restraint`: Do not bold every proper noun or acronym.
- `inline-header-list-convert`: Turn bullets whose bold label merely restates the line into prose, keeping a period-ended label followed by new detail.
- `sentence-case-headings`: Write headings in sentence case.
- `no-decorative-emoji`: Remove ornamental emoji from headings and bullets.
- `straight-quotes`: Replace typographic quotation marks with straight ones.

#### core · X · Continuity — beads
- `bead-type-taxonomy`: Use only the six bead types (epic, feature, task, bug, spike, decision) and the single human label, never inventing others.
- `field-roles`: Give each bead field its single job — description, design, acceptance, spec_id, notes, comments and close reason — and never overload one.
- `wait-as-edge`: Record every wait as an explicit edge — a blocks dependency, a human task, or a gate — written in the needs direction so ready-work stays truthful.
- `actor-identity`: Carry one stable actor for the whole session, claiming on start and acting only on your own claims.
- `resume-line`: On pause or handoff, unclaim and append a resume line naming the approach to resume with and where the work stands.
- `session-close`: Close a session by closing finished beads with evidence, unclaiming the rest with resume lines, running the gates, refreshing the export, and reporting.
- `session-recovery`: At session start or after compaction, list in-progress beads and resume from each one's last note.
- `knowledge-in-files`: Keep durable knowledge in files, never in the tracker's remember, memories or key-value stores.
- `beads-setup`: Install the tracker, adopt it in a project, and join from a new clone with bootstrap rather than a re-init.
- `status-model`: Drive status through the model's own transitions — the custom review status, deferred as the whole backlog, and never a hand-set blocked.
- `triage-routing`: Route each triaged item to one outcome expressed in the tracker's native fields (admit with acceptance, hand to a human task, defer, reject, or mark duplicate) with no separate intake labels.
- `durable-unit-scope`: Track one durable unit of work per bead, keeping turn checklists out, searching before creating, and filing incidental finds as discovered-from beads.
- `review-as-task`: Represent a review as its own task by an actor other than the author, which the reviewed bead depends on and sits in review status until it passes.
- `destructive-command-guard`: Never run the tracker's deleting commands, reclaiming space with a non-destructive compact instead.
- `repeated-procedures`: Capture short repeated runs as disposable wisps and fixed multi-step procedures as poured formulas, checking what the tracker actually parsed.
- `dolt-sync`: Treat the versioned database as the source of truth and the exported jsonl as a review mirror, syncing copies only with authority.

#### core · X · Continuity — decision-trail
- `single-tsv-decision-log`: Keep one authoritative decision log as a single TSV file with one single-line row per decision.
- `evidence-pointer-cell`: Make a row's evidence cell a resolvable pointer such as a commit, pull request, file and line or artifact path, never narrative.
- `trail-six-columns`: Give every row the fixed columns ts in ISO8601, phase or workstream, the decision in one line, why, evidence, and result as an outcome or state.
- `caller-trail-columns`: Let a caller add declared columns after a trail's fixed ones, the same set on every call.
- `plain-row-wording`: Write rows the way you would tell a colleague, in concrete words, spelling a guiding principle out in place of citing it as a tag.
- `named-cell-row-helper`: Append rows through a helper that takes named cells and declared extra columns, and writes nothing when a cell is missing, unknown or undeclared.
- `decision-points-only`: Log decision points and checkpoints (a chosen fork, a finished unit with its verification, a pivot or revert with its cause, a surfaced blocker, a fixed gate), never each action or a self-evident step.
- `row-per-iteration`: Have a looping run write one row for each iteration.
- `creates-log-parent`: Have the log helper create a missing parent directory.
- `locked-single-header`: Hold an exclusive lock across reading and appending, so simultaneous first writers make one header and rows never interleave.
- `append-mode-writes`: Write the header and rows only in append mode, so a false empty-file test costs a stray header and never the rows.
- `automatic-utc-stamp`: Have the log helper stamp each row with the current UTC time so the caller supplies none.
- `cell-whitespace-strip`: Replace tabs, newlines and carriage returns in each cell with spaces.
- `numeric-safe-formula-quote`: Quote a cell starting with a character a spreadsheet parses as a formula, unless it is a plain signed number or percentage.
- `run-boundary`: Count one agent conversation with its later turns and summaries as one run, and a pickup, replacement agent or new chat as a new one.
- `start-row-triggers`: Have a run adding to a log with rows write a `start` row first, and on returning read the log's tail and write a fresh one if another run's `start` has appeared.
- `start-row-contents`: Have a `start` row name the timestamp range of the rows this run did not write and identify this run in its evidence, using the `start` phase for nothing else.
- `trail-location-rule`: Keep a trail at the caller's path, else at an ignored scratch path by slug, else in Git's own directory, and outside Git in the working folder, saying so in the reply.
- `proposed-trail-commit`: Propose committing a trail only when a reviewer needs it to trust the outcome, and commit only with authority.
- `append-only-supersede`: Never edit or delete a ledger record; correct or reverse one by appending a record that supersedes it.
- `end-of-run-audit`: Before handing back, check the log for truthfulness against what happened in the run.
- `no-cross-project-transcript-search`: Never search across project transcript folders during an audit, because that exposes unrelated private conversations.
- `audit-own-stretches`: Limit an audit to this run's row stretches, each from one of its `start` rows or the log's first row to the next `start` row of another run.
- `verified-record-row-walk`: Check each audited row against a real event only in an event record the caller names, verified and scoped to this workspace.
- `evidence-resolves-check`: Check that each audited row's pointer resolves and supports what the row says.
- `unlogged-fork-gap`: Treat a fork, pivot or abandoned path that shaped the work with no row as a gap, and add the row in the audit.
- `audit-supersedes-in-place-of-editing`: Have an audit change no row, even an invented one, and add a row superseding it with what really happened and a pointer that resolves.
- `foreign-row-on-own-evidence`: Supersede a row outside the audited stretches only when this run's own work shows it to be wrong.
- `same-family-or-unreviewed`: Have a critic from another model family review the trail before hand-back, one of the same family only with the owner's approval, and otherwise report it not reviewed, never reviewing your own run.
- `evidence-pointer-review`: Give a trail's critic the trail and the evidence each row points at, or the trail and a verified workspace-scoped record when one is named.
- `attention-scan-not-redo`: Have the trail's reviewer look for what is suboptimal or risky for the user's attention and not repeat the work.
- `trail-review-flags`: Have the trail's reviewer flag weak or absent evidence, checks skipped or claimed without proof, choices risky in hindsight, and gaps a casual read would miss.
- `attention-with-coverage`: End a reply with Attention naming the reviewer or `not reviewed` with its reason, each flag with its rows or no flags, and, after an evidence-pointer review, transcript coverage and unlogged-fork detection as unavailable.
- `script-evidence-preference`: Favour evidence generated by committed scripts over hand-made one-off evidence.

#### core · X · Continuity — recall
- `current-state-capsule-goal`: Rebuild recent working context into a compact statement of the present position and what comes next.
- `two-record-context-model`: Treat context as living in both the agent's own chat history and a shared record of tracker, chat, docs, source control and error reports.
- `recall-routes-away`: First rule out resuming one known chat, making a durable skill from habits and writing a human-facing work summary, since those are other tasks.
- `skip-mining-with-supplied-state`: If the user already gave paths, branch and the change, use that and do no mining.
- `lock-scope-before-search`: Fix the time window, topic and workspace before any searching, and say the locked scope to the user.
- `seven-day-default-window`: Treat recent as a real range with a default of seven days.
- `active-workspace-only-default`: Default to the current workspace and read another project's chats only when asked.
- `no-silent-narrowing`: Never quietly reduce a request for everything into a recent subset.
- `order-by-real-mtime`: Sort candidates by actual modification time, never by identifier name.
- `grep-then-read-matching-regions`: Search for the topic first, then open only chats that match and only the parts of them that bear on it.
- `exclude-current-and-noise-chats`: Leave out the current chat along with subagent, evaluation and test chats.
- `uniform-per-chat-schema`: Require from each subagent one block per chat recording topic, goal, decisions, unresolved threads, difficulties, corrections and produced artifacts.
- `finding-cited-by-source-kind`: Cite chat findings by chat identifier and shared-record findings by pull request, ticket, permalink or error-tracker issue.
- `direct-search-for-small-corpus`: With one or two chats, search directly without fanning out.
- `default-shared-record-sweep`: Search the shared record by default when a feature, file, subsystem, area or bug is named, omitting it only for activity recall with no named target.
- `one-helper-per-sizeable-source`: Give a shared-record source its own helper only when its investigation is sizeable and independent, and read small sources directly.
- `retarget-investigator-question`: Change the investigators' question from design rationale to current state, failed attempts and ongoing user reports.
- `empty-search-is-finding`: Count a search that returned nothing as a result to report, not as work to discard.
- `full-transcript-for-agent-behaviour`: When the answer depends on what an agent actually did, read the complete transcript and not a trimmed local copy.
- `brief-grouped-by-thread`: Organize a recall brief by thread and stay on the named topic.
- `brief-section-order`: Present capsule, thread status, problems and next move in that order, with further detail below or cut.
- `capped-capsule-section`: Hold the opening capsule to five bullets at most.
- `status-tagged-thread-lines-with-abandoned`: Give each thread one line with one tag from merged, open pull request, in flight, verified uncommitted, reverted, abandoned or planned, describing any other state in plain words.
- `capped-recurring-problems`: List at most five recurring problems, including persistent user symptoms and reverted fixes, so the next try starts from the last failure.
- `single-next-move`: End with the one most useful concrete next action.
- `adjacent-excluded-unless-blocking`: Leave out a neighbouring feature or ticket unless it blocks this one.
- `cut-detail-before-threads`: When a recall brief passes a screen, remove detail ahead of removing threads.
- `reply-is-the-deliverable`: Return the deliverable itself as the reply, never an account of what was done to produce it.

#### core · X · Continuity — wake
- `run-card-limits`: Hold a run's deadline, attempts, closed state and checkpoint in a card at a fresh path under a unique run id, refusing without them.
- `one-consuming-admit`: Count work once, by the caller, immediately before the unit; every other query changes nothing, and only exit 0 authorises work.
- `one-closing-timer`: Set at most one one-shot timer, at or after the deadline and only for a stated unattended run, and record the time the surface says it fires.
- `timer-positive-evidence`: Report a timer set only on the surface's named evidence; a listed tool alone is not evidence and uncertain means unavailable.
- `timer-identity-check`: On a timer fire ask the card only whether this run is open; a closed or other run does nothing, and everything else is the caller's closing step.
- `timer-close-cancels`: Close the card and cancel the timer on every exit, naming a cancel that failed.
- `woken-run-limits`: While a card is open: no push, publish, merge, message or history rewrite, no deleting what this run did not create, no costly opt-in the request does not name, and a missing answer takes the unit's no-answer exit without skipping its core.

#### core · X · Coordination — delegation
- `role-contracts`: Give each delegated role a fixed contract of access, duties and report shape, and carry it inside the brief because the worker may not load the delegating instructions.
- `no-onward-delegation`: A delegated worker does not hand its work on to further agents unless its brief allows it.
- `preserve-role-prompt`: Keep role behaviour in one role prompt independent of the runtime metadata applied around it at invocation.
- `owner-roster`: Take each role's vendor, model and settings from the owner's roster, let a model the owner names override it for one dispatch, and ask the owner when neither exists rather than choosing.
- `cross-family-review`: Have work reviewed by a model from a different family than its author's, and get the owner's explicit approval before a same-family review.
- `vendor-model-list`: Take the selectable models and efforts from each vendor's own source (its live catalog, or a list generated from its command or API), falling back to a reviewed, sourced seed only when no such source is reachable.
- `model-list-freshness`: Refuse a generated model list when the vendor fetch behind it is missing or older than the allowed age, timing it by the vendor's fetch rather than by when the list was written.
- `validate-selection`: Validate every selected spawn dimension deterministically before spawning, rejecting any value the catalog does not declare rather than substituting a nearby one.
- `vendor-owned-dispatch`: Dispatch through the chosen vendor's own tools and follow their rules, adding no process around a vendor's own orchestrator.
- `capable-native-subagent`: Use the harness's own subagent tool only when it can run the chosen model with its settings.
- `effective-run-record`: Record the model and settings a vendor reports actually ran for a dispatch, marking any it does not report as requested-but-unverified.
- `enforced-read-only`: Keep a read-only role read-only with the vendor's enforced control, such as a sandbox or tool list, where one exists, and state when the brief is the only control.
- `session-resume-followup`: Send a follow-up to a worker by resuming its own session rather than starting a fresh one.
- `codex-direct`: Call the Codex CLI directly rather than through the retired adapter plugin.
- `closed-stdin`: Close standard input when running an agent CLI non-interactively so it cannot wait for input with no timeout.
- `result-error-check`: Judge an agent CLI run by its structured result's error flag, never by its exit code alone.
- `background-dispatch-for-dialogue`: Run subagents in the background so the coordinator stays in live dialogue with the user.
- `brief-names-done-evidence`: A brief names what will show the work is finished, and a unit with nothing to name is scoped further or raised with the owner before dispatch.
- `read-worker-output`: Open the diff or artifact a worker produced and hold it to the evidence its brief named, instead of relying on its summary.
- `stalled-worker-by-output`: Stop or replace a worker that stalls or loops, judging it by what it has produced rather than its status text.
- `retry-by-cause`: Retry a failed worker according to why it failed, with a narrower unit, the same brief or another model, and after two retries drop the unit and plan around it.
- `fresh-context-subagent`: Start every subagent in a fresh context window rather than as a copy of the caller's conversation.

#### core · X · Coordination — model-council
- `member-resolution`: Resolve the members and judge from the request's explicit selections, asking only for missing choices or unreachable members.
- `runtime-capability-check`: Verify actual runtime dispatch interfaces before assuming cross-provider access from a model name or placing effort only in prose when a runtime control exists.
- `neutral-framing`: Frame one neutral shared brief for every member, stating the question, constraints and uncertainty with no preferred conclusion.
- `member-isolation`: Give each member the shared brief in isolation so none sees another's response; sequential dispatch is allowed.
- `report-preservation`: Save every member's full attributed report under the run directory rather than discarding it after synthesis.
- `independent-synthesis`: A fresh synthesizer that did not participate receives every member's full report and produces agreement, disputes, blind spots and a best-supported recommendation, treating agreement as no proof.
- `consolidated-delivery`: Deliver a concise consolidation with member-position summaries and paths to every full report, inlining full text only on request.
- `identity-recording`: Record the actual model identities wherever the runtime provides evidence of them.
- `failed-member-recovery`: Give a failed member bounded safe recovery before treating it as missing.
- `no-silent-substitution`: Never backfill a missing member with your own answer or a silent substitute; report the gap and whether the synthesizer saw an incomplete set.
- `artifact-named-up-front`: State exactly what artifact each candidate must produce before any candidate starts.
- `task-rubric-criteria`: Write three to six concrete, gradeable success criteria specific to this task.
- `rubric-withheld-from-candidates`: Keep the success criteria from the candidates, who see only the task.
- `own-output-location`: Give every candidate or adversary a separate output location, so they share no writable state.
- `rationale-names-rejected`: Have each candidate deliver, with its artifact, a short rationale naming the alternatives it weighed and what it rejected.
- `dropout-proceeds-noted`: Go on with the remaining candidates or adversaries when one produces nothing, and record the dropout.
- `read-only-judge`: Give the judge read-only access.
- `judge-other-family-or-stated`: Take the judge from a model family other than the coordinator's, and say so when the user's choice shares that family or the coordinator cannot tell its own.
- `rubric-given-to-judge`: Give the judge the success criteria to score against.
- `path-labelled-candidates`: Show the judge each candidate under its path label.
- `judge-criterion-scores`: Have the judge score each candidate on each criterion.
- `judge-recommends-base`: Have the judge recommend a base and justify the recommendation.
- `full-read-before-pick`: Read every candidate in full before choosing a base.
- `picker-criterion-scores`: Score each candidate on each criterion instead of by overall impression.
- `pick-compared-with-judge`: Compare your scored pick with the judge's, treating the same choice as confirmation.
- `disagreement-rereads-rationales`: Treat a disagreement with the judge as a sign of bias or an unclear rubric, and read both rationales before deciding.
- `base-chosen-for-extensibility`: Choose the base a later maintainer could extend most easily while keeping invariants intact.
- `near-tie-smaller-surface`: Break a near-tie in favour of the cleaner boundary or the smaller interface.
- `loser-graft-pass`: Go through each losing candidate once more for parts worth carrying over.
- `sparse-grafts`: Expect only one or two grafts from a losing candidate, not the bulk of it.
- `hand-folded-grafts`: Rewrite each graft into the base by hand, so the result keeps one coherent design rather than pasted fragments.
- `converged-shape-no-graft`: When candidates reach one shape, record the agreement and ship that shape with no graft.
- `divergence-reframes-once`: When candidates differ wildly, treat the frame as too loose, reframe and rerun at most once, then stop and report instead of blending them.
- `graft-change-rerun`: After grafting, rerun the acceptance check of any previously checked behaviour the graft changed, reuse evidence for the rest and name what stays unchecked.
- `verify-miss-returns-once`: Send a verification problem back once to reframing or to grafting, whichever caused it, then report any further miss rather than hiding it.
- `single-synthesized-artifact`: End with one merged artifact rather than a set of alternatives.
- `synthesis-decision-record`: Record the chosen base candidate with its reason, what was grafted from the rest and why each was rejected.
- `note-judge-status`: Record in the synthesis note the judge's verdict or that the judge was skipped.
- `note-convergence-dropouts`: Record any convergence or dropped candidates in the synthesis note.
- `note-verification-result`: Record the verification result in the synthesis note.
- `no-judge-no-pick`: With no judge reachable, count no completed council: stop, say so and return the candidates with no pick.

#### core · X · Coordination — mvp-mode
