#### core · Intake · Clarification — skill:pstack/skills/in-your-own-words
- `goal-and-problem-restatement`: Say in your own wording what you believe the user is aiming for and which problem they are trying to solve. — adopt → restate#goal-and-problem-restatement

#### core · Intake · Clarification — skill:pstack/skills/sharpen
- `depth-not-scope-rewrite`: Treat improving a task as making it deeper, and refuse to make it merely larger. — adopt → sharpen#depth-not-scope-rewrite
- `diagnose-then-rewrite-prompt`: Answer a fixed set of diagnostic questions first, then rewrite the prompt to ask for exactly what they revealed. — adopt → sharpen#diagnose-then-rewrite-prompt
- `expert-gap-question`: Say what a leading practitioner would do here that the request leaves out. — adopt → sharpen#expert-gap-question
- `rawest-source-question`: Name the least processed material a practitioner would begin from in place of the summarized input. — adopt → sharpen#rawest-source-question
- `expert-methods-question`: Name the concrete techniques and instruments a practitioner would apply. — adopt → sharpen#expert-methods-question
- `outside-correctness-signal`: Name something outside both the agent and the user that would show the result is correct. — adopt → sharpen#outside-correctness-signal
- `owner-choices-left-open`: Keep decisions that belong to the user unresolved when rewriting their request. — adopt → sharpen#owner-choices-left-open

#### core · Intake · Triage — skill:pstack/automations/benny/skills/triage-issue-reports
- `triage-never-reproduces`: Limit triage to classifying one report, posting one verdict and filing only clear new bugs, never reproducing or fixing. — reject
- `fail-closed-run-config`: Stop a run before any write when its configuration or a required tool or map is missing, malformed or incomplete. — defer
- `frozen-source-coordinates`: Read and check the source channel and thread of a report once, before any work list or delegation, and never change or replace them for the rest of the run. — defer
- `no-root-post-in-source`: Post in the source channel only as a reply inside the report's thread, never as a new top-level message. — defer
- `no-cross-post`: Never post to another channel, broadcast, message privately or start a new thread, and point a misdirected reporter to the right place inside their own thread. — defer
- `thread-parent-preflight`: Before each write tied to a report thread, re-read the thread to confirm its parent message still exists in the same channel, and after posting confirm the reply landed, never falling back to another place. — defer
- `single-verdict-reply`: Post one verdict and no progress messages, leading with the outcome, linking any issue, naming a reroute or one missing fact, with at most one allowed ping and one marker line. — defer
- `coordinator-only-chat-writes`: Let only the coordinating agent write to chat, telling every worker in its brief that chat writes are forbidden and giving it no means to make them. — defer
- `findings-only-read-only-workers`: Give each delegated analysis worker one narrow question, no write access and no chat credentials, and take back findings only. — defer
- `worker-isolation-or-coordinator`: Hand work to a worker only where its environment provably enforces the run's write limits, and otherwise have the coordinator do that work itself. — defer
- `strict-issue-create-gate`: File an issue only for a clearly broken, still-live bug or performance report with no live match, a passing preflight, resolved fields and a link back to the source, preferring no ticket to a guessed or duplicate one. — defer
- `whole-report-thread-read`: Read a report's opening message and every reply so far before deciding on it. — defer
- `report-fact-capture`: Collect a fixed set of facts from a bug report before deciding on it: the reporter's words, version and environment, expected and observed behaviour, frequency and trigger, error signatures, attachments, links and any claim that someone already owns it. — defer
- `inspect-attachments-admit-unreadable`: Read every relevant screenshot, video and log closely, and name an attachment that could not be read rather than guess at it. — defer
- `self-serve-facts`: Look up available facts yourself rather than asking, leaving only the decisions to the live participant. — reject
- `routing-cause-trace`: Before routing, run a bounded trace from action to result that checks where the symptom belongs, recent changes and existing fixes, deep enough to avoid misrouting but not a full root cause, and say tracing was unavailable when the code cannot be read. — defer
- `five-way-report-classes`: Give each report exactly one class: bug, performance (kept as a bug with its measurements), feature request, question or feedback, or reroute, filing nothing when bug versus feature is unclear. — reject
- `evidence-based-routing`: Match a report to a route only on evidence of its product area, code path or error signature, using stable keys and never the visible symptom or a keyword alone. — defer
- `no-guessed-route`: Without a matching route, classify but name no destination or owner, and keep the fallback empty unless one team accepts everything unmatched. — defer
- `route-map-schema`: Describe each route by name, match lists, destination, owners and whether its feature owner may be pinged. — defer
- `owner-ping-gate`: Keep owner pings off by default and allow one only to a configured feature owner who agreed or a confirmed regression author, never a broad on-call group or an unverified owner. — defer
- `tracker-adapter-contract`: Require a tracker adapter that searches, reads, creates, updates without clobbering, adds links and recurrence notes and undoes its own issue, failing closed per missing operation and inventing no field value. — defer
- `already-handled-check`: Post and create nothing when the report's link is already tied to an issue or a prior triage reply. — defer
- `tracker-duplicate-search`: Search the tracker for an existing issue that describes the same fault before deciding on a bug report. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → triage#tracker-duplicate-search
- `duplicate-search-key-list`: Run the duplicate search over a fixed list of keys, among them the error signature, the area, the trigger, the symptom, a version window, the suspected commit and the source link. — reject
- `graded-duplicate-match`: Grade each search hit as a confident duplicate, possibly related or no match, marking only a confident one as a duplicate and linking a possible one without acting on it. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → triage#graded-duplicate-match
- `closed-match-is-regression-lead`: Treat a long-closed issue that matches a new report as a lead to a regression, not as a live duplicate. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → triage#fixed-match-regression-lead
- `issue-template-and-title`: Write a new issue as a self-contained record with a plain area-and-symptom title that never states a guessed cause, the reporter's words, expected and observed behaviour, version, trigger, frequency, link, labelled hypotheses and media. — reject
- `trusted-verdict-marker`: Pass a report from triage to repair through a fixed one-line marker that repair accepts only from the configured triage identity, in the same thread, and only for a bug or performance verdict. — defer
- `compensate-orphan-issue`: If the run created an issue and its verdict did not land, cancel or remove that issue and confirm it, reporting any unconfirmed undo in the run output. — defer
- `bounded-follow-up-window`: After the main reply, watch the thread for one bounded window, answering only direct questions, staying out of side chatter and stopping when asked. — defer
- `follow-up-safe-issue-corrections`: During a follow-up window, safely correct the existing or new tracker issue linked to the report, emit no second marker, extend the window at most once and leave new reports to new runs. — defer
- `secret-containment`: Keep secrets and private data out of any destination not authorized to hold them. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md

#### core · Building · Implementation — skill:pstack/skills/principle-build-the-lever
- `tool-over-hand-work`: For non-trivial edits, analyses or checks, write a rerunnable tool that does or proves the work, so a reviewer reruns it instead of trusting a hand-made result. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `hand-first-recipe`: Do the first unit by hand, then build the tool and show it reproduces the hand result before running it on the rest. — adopt → build-a-lever#hand-first-recipe
- `rerun-safe-tool`: Make a work tool safe to rerun on input it has already changed. — adopt → build-a-lever#rerun-safe-tool
- `script-over-fanout`: When one deterministic pass can process every unit, run a script rather than fanning the units out to delegates. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `shared-delegate-contract`: When fanning work out, give every delegate one shared artifact with the recipe, the verification contract and the fences, kept outside their write scope. — defer
- `outliving-tool-commit`: Commit a work tool when the work it does outlives the session. — adopt → build-a-lever#proposed-artifact-commit
- `minimal-tool`: Build the smallest script that does or proves the job, never a framework. — adopt → build-a-lever#minimal-tool

#### core · Verification · Review — skill:pstack/skills/blast-radius
- `breakage-beyond-callers`: Spend the effort on breakage text search cannot reveal, not on listing callers. — adopt → review#breakage-beyond-callers
- `safety-fact-proved-by-run`: Treat a convincing writeup as worthless by itself, and prove the fact a change's safety rests on by running real code and including what happened. — adopt → review#safety-fact-proved-by-run
- `evidence-ladder`: Grade each safety-bearing fact as asserted, cited to a line, failure walked through, executed in a script or test, or reproduced in the running product. — adopt → review#evidence-ladder
- `ladder-as-far-as-cheap`: Take each fact as far up the evidence ladder as is cheap and state where it stopped. — adopt → review#ladder-as-far-as-cheap
- `small-real-library-script`: Normally reach the executed level with one short script that imports the library shipped with the product and calls exactly the function at issue. — adopt → review#small-real-library-script
- `failing-loud-proof`: Make a proof script or test fail noisily if the claim is wrong. — adopt → review#failing-loud-proof
- `whole-change-including-unstated`: Go through the diff, the symbols added, changed and deleted, and the behaviour change the diff does not spell out. — adopt → review#whole-change-including-unstated
- `change-history-pull`: Retrieve the related pull request and commits while reading a change. — adopt → review#change-history-pull
- `single-safety-fact-search`: Find the one fact that makes a change safe and clears most risky cases, and spend the time there, not on a long list of possibilities. — adopt → review#single-safety-fact-search
- `dependency-source-and-pin`: Read the called library's source and confirm its pinned version and whether it is locally patched. — adopt → review#dependency-source-and-pin
- `timing-and-lifecycle-analysis`: Work out when things execute, including deferred callbacks, teardown and framework differences. — adopt → review#timing-and-lifecycle-analysis
- `non-symbol-coupling-trace`: Follow links symbol search misses: returned data shapes, database columns, wire formats, another language reading the same bytes, feature flags and code several hops away. — adopt → review#non-symbol-coupling-trace
- `likelihood-and-cost-per-risk`: Give each risk an honest probability and an honest cost. — adopt → review#likelihood-and-cost-per-risk
- `confirmed-and-cleared-split`: Keep confirmed risks apart from those checked and cleared, saying why each cleared one is fine. — adopt → review#confirmed-and-cleared-split
- `empty-search-is-finding`: Count a search that returned nothing as a result to report, not as work to discard. — adopt → review#empty-search-is-finding
- `no-fabrication`: Never fabricate citations, data or examples. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `multi-model-question-on-wide-change`: For a big or wide change, put the same question to more than one model and merge the answers. — reject
- `handback-what-it-does`: Say what changed, including the non-obvious part. — adopt → review#handback-what-it-does
- `handback-safety-fact-with-grade`: State the safety fact, its ladder level and its proof, or mark it unproven. — adopt → review#handback-safety-fact-with-grade
- `handback-risk-fields`: For each risk give how it breaks, the actual file and line, likelihood and severity, how to check it, and the proof for those that matter. — adopt → review#handback-risk-fields
- `handback-pre-merge-check`: Give the cheapest test or reproduction able to expose the actual bug, along with any script written. — adopt → review#handback-pre-merge-check
- `secret-containment`: Keep secrets and private data out of any destination not authorized to hold them. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md

#### core · Verification · Review — skill:pstack/skills/interrogate
- `break-it-mandate`: Assign adversaries to try to break a change or design rather than assess it in general. — adopt → interrogate#break-it-mandate
- `run-proven-finding`: Let a finding stand only when a run executed in the review shows it, so a claim nobody ran is no finding. — adopt → interrogate#run-proven-finding
- `inspection-only-authority`: Treat a review or analysis request as authority to inspect and report only, never to change the work. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `named-scope-first`: Use the scope the user names when one is given. — adopt → interrogate#named-scope-first
- `merge-base-through-tree-scope`: When no scope is named, review the branch from where it left the base branch up to and including the working tree. — defer
- `intent-restated-first`: Restate the change's intent in your own words before sending out adversaries. — adopt → interrogate#intent-restated-first
- `intent-from-request-commits-pr`: Derive the intent from the request, the commits and the pull request description. — adopt → interrogate#intent-from-stated-sources
- `ask-when-intent-unclear`: Ask the user when the intent cannot be established. — adopt → interrogate#ask-or-not-run-on-intent
- `role-model-config-line`: Read each spawned role's model from a named line of a shared configuration, falling back to a fixed default and leaving the field unset for an alias. — reject
- `own-output-location`: Give every candidate or adversary a separate output location, so they share no writable state. — adopt → interrogate#own-output-location
- `one-message-fan-out`: Launch every candidate or adversary in one message as background subagents. — reject
- `dropout-proceeds-noted`: Go on with the remaining candidates or adversaries when one produces nothing, and record the dropout. — adopt → interrogate#dropout-proceeds-noted
- `uncommitted-changes-seeded`: Seed every adversary workspace with the uncommitted work included in the review scope. — adopt → interrogate#verified-snapshot-copy
- `general-purpose-adversary`: Spawn each adversary as the general-purpose subagent type. — reject
- `adversary-fixed-brief`: Hand every adversary the scope, the intent and one unchanging instruction to break the work, replacing the usual task and rationale request. — adopt → interrogate#adversaries-by-model-or-angle
- `run-against-real-code`: Require each finding to be demonstrated by executing something against the actual code, such as a failing test, a reproduction script or revealing command output. — adopt → interrogate#run-against-real-code
- `design-proof-by-probe`: For a design or plan, prove a finding by running a prototype or probing the current tree. — adopt → interrogate#design-proof-by-probe
- `repros-stay-in-copy`: Keep each adversary's reproduction material inside its own output location. — adopt → interrogate#repros-stay-in-copy
- `finding-repro-report`: Require each finding to carry a title, the exact command, the printed output and the output the intent requires. — adopt → interrogate#finding-repro-report
- `style-findings-excluded`: Leave style, naming and structure out of an adversary's findings. — reject
- `future-change-risk-excluded`: Leave out hazards that matter only after a future change. — reject
- `no-findings-valid`: Accept a report with no findings as a valid result, and say so explicitly when none remain. — adopt → interrogate#no-findings-valid
- `coordinator-replays-finding`: Have the coordinator verify each finding by running its command again. — adopt → interrogate#coordinator-replays-finding
- `reproduced-and-breaks-intent`: Keep a finding only if the output shows the failure and that failure breaks the stated intent. — adopt → interrogate#reproduced-and-breaks-intent
- `drop-unverified-findings`: Remove every finding that fails the keep test. — adopt → interrogate#three-replay-outcomes
- `merge-by-root-cause`: Combine findings that share one root cause. — adopt → interrogate#merge-by-root-cause
- `no-judge-pick-or-graft`: Omit judging, base selection and grafting from a review by adversaries. — reject
- `union-of-verified-findings`: Keep every verified finding across adversaries rather than selecting one adversary's list. — adopt → interrogate#union-of-verified-findings
- `output-opens-with-intent`: Open the output with the intent restatement. — adopt → interrogate#output-opens-with-intent
- `output-finding-fields`: For each verified finding, report its command, its output and how it breaks the intent. — adopt → interrogate#output-finding-fields
- `adversary-attribution`: Name the adversaries that found each verified finding. — adopt → interrogate#adversary-attribution
- `dropped-finding-accounting`: Report for each adversary how many findings were dropped and why. — adopt → interrogate#dropped-finding-accounting

#### core · Verification · Review — skill:pstack/skills/no-comments
- `merge-base-through-tree-scope`: When no scope is named, review the branch from where it left the base branch up to and including the working tree. — adopt → no-comments#merge-base-through-tree-scope
- `named-scope-first`: Use the scope the user names when one is given. — adopt → no-comments#named-scope-first
- `comment-critic-role`: Spawn a fixed subagent role to audit comments and pass it the scope. — reject
- `defer-to-fresh-critic`: Give weight to a critic's fresh perspective over the caller's own attachment. — reject
- `role-rules-not-restated`: Do not repeat a spawned role's rules in the request that spawns it. — reject
- `job-fit-helper-effort`: Choose each helper's thinking depth and speed tier to suit its job. — reject
- `read-worker-output`: Open the diff or artifact a worker produced and hold it to the evidence its brief named, instead of relying on its summary. — reject
- `critic-out-of-bounds-refused`: Refuse a critic's edits to application code and any of its work outside the given scope. — adopt → no-comments#comment-pass-stays-in-bounds
- `comment-exception-gate`: Refuse deleting a comment a stated exception protects, and bring one back only with that exact exception and proof within scope. — adopt → principle-no-comments#exact-proof-settles-a-protected-keep
- `misstated-kill-reason-refused`: Refuse a report whose reason for a mandatory comment deletion is wrong. — reject
- `kept-code-not-guilty`: Refuse flags that treat intentionally retained code as being at fault. — adopt → no-comments#kept-code-not-guilty
- `reshape-flags-stay-open`: Keep flags asking to restructure surprising first-party code open, without bringing their comments back. — adopt → no-comments#reshape-flags-open-apart-from-comment
- `comment-keep-needs-proof`: Let a comment survive only with proof it concerns something the team cannot alter. — adopt → principle-no-comments#unsure-comment-kept-and-flagged
- `missed-suppression-audit`: Check the scope for lint and type-checker suppression comments the critic overlooked. — adopt → no-comments#suppressions-in-comment-sweep
- `safety-suppressions-removed`: Treat suppressions bearing on correctness or safety as findings that must be removed. — adopt → principle-no-comments#safety-suppressions-removed
- `thin-importance-comment-check`: Before accepting a thinly justified decision on a comment marked important, investigate its symbol's behaviour and history. — adopt → no-comments#thin-importance-comment-check
- `ambiguous-comment-deleted`: Leave an ambiguous deletion deleted, and delete a kept comment that is refuted or stays ambiguous. — adopt → principle-no-comments#unsure-comment-kept-and-flagged
- `one-named-rerun-then-fail`: After rejecting a report, revert it and rerun the critic once with the failure named, and fail the run if the second report is rejected too. — reject
- `trivial-flag-direct-fix`: Resolve simple accepted flags at once through edits such as removing an unused path or parameter, or calling the genuine interface. — adopt → no-comments#trivial-flag-direct-fix
- `one-sketch-for-accepted-set`: When a fix needs a design, run one design pass over all accepted flags and nearby code, stopping at the sketch and leaving implementation to a later step. — reject
- `smallest-in-scope-root-cause-fix`: Implement the smallest in-scope fix for the underlying cause, and when the cause lies beyond scope land that fix and list the rest as open. — reject
- `named-workarounds-removed`: Eliminate every workaround the findings name. — adopt → no-comments#named-workarounds-removed
- `principles-never-widen-scope`: Treat guiding principles as intent only, never permission to expand the boundary or fix other instances. — reject
- `no-symptom-guards`: Never add a guard that merely masks a symptom. — reject
- `constraint-comment-class`: Treat comments that forbid removal, forbid rewording or require consulting someone as a distinct class. — adopt → principle-no-comments#constraint-comment-class
- `unchangeable-constraint-kept`: Leave kept comments that concern things outside the team's control. — adopt → principle-no-comments#unchangeable-constraint-kept
- `cheapest-enforcement-offer`: For other constraint comments, propose the least costly enforcement available in scope, whether a type, runtime check, test or CI lint. — adopt → no-comments#cheapest-enforcement-offer
- `encoding-approval-gate`: Apply an encoding only with approval, through the route the caller names or given by the caller in advance. — adopt → no-comments#encoding-approval-gate
- `encode-then-delete`: When an encoding is approved, add the enforcement and then remove the comment. — adopt → no-comments#encode-then-delete
- `unencoded-constraint-reported`: Without approval, delete the comment, report the constraint as open and sketch any out-of-scope work. — adopt → no-comments#unencoded-constraint-kept-and-reported
- `comment-audit-report`: Report the counts of comments deleted and restored, reruns, the sketch, fixes, encodings offered and done, constraints left unenforced and open items. — adopt → no-comments#comment-sweep-report

#### core · Verification · Validation — skill:pstack/skills/principle-prove-it-works
- `direct-observation`: Verify a result by observing the real thing (run it, read the actual value, check liveness directly), never a proxy, a cached view or a self-report. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `suspect-the-observation`: When a check fails unexpectedly, test the observation method before concluding the system is wrong. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `scripted-proof`: Prefer a deterministic, rerunnable script as the proof of a result, and keep its output for a reviewer. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `audit-trail-proof-commit`: Keep a proof artifact visible to the human, and commit it only when large or complex work needs an auditable trail. — adopt → build-a-lever#proposed-artifact-commit

#### core · Improvement · Codification — skill:pstack/skills/automate-me
- `persona-update-or-fresh`: Find an existing working-style skill for the person and confirm whether to update it, the default, or start fresh, asking why before starting fresh. — defer
- `incremental-persona-update`: In update mode, mine only history since the skill's last commit, ask what changed, and edit the file in place keeping sections nothing contradicts. — defer
- `no-cross-project-transcript-search`: Never search across project transcript folders during an audit, because that exposes unrelated private conversations. — adopt → reflect#no-cross-project-transcript-search
- `sliced-parallel-history-mining`: Mine recent history with parallel helpers, each taking one time slice and returning a short structured list of patterns with pointers to evidence. — defer
- `working-style-signal-checklist`: Look for a fixed set of working-style signals and group them into fixed sections: reply style, autonomy, understanding first, helpers, prose and code discipline, review, process and skills. — defer
- `corroborated-patterns-only`: Codify a preference only when it recurs across separate stretches of history, dropping a lone or later-contradicted signal. — defer
- `structured-choice-interview`: Ask the person one or two structured questions with four to six options, broad before specific, then one open question. — reject
- `granularity-reference-only`: Read an existing working-style skill for its level of detail only, never copying its content. — defer
- `persona-skill-placement`: Place the generated skill in an existing category, else a personal folder the repo has, else a project mode folder, or the person's own skills folder on request. — defer
- `persona-skill-frontmatter`: Give the generated skill a description that triggers on the person's name and style, written as one YAML scalar, and make it manual unless wanted every turn. — defer
- `trigger-tuning-on-observed-miss`: Tune a skill's description in a loop only after its triggering has been shown to fail in use. — defer
- `iterate-draft-and-cut`: Show the draft over several feedback rounds and cut it hard. — defer
- `skill-lands-via-branch-and-pr`: Land a skill from a worktree off main with a commit and pull request, never a direct push. — reject
- `operational-agent-prose`: Write agent-facing text operationally, with no restating of other skills, metaphors or poetic prose. — reject
- `reference-other-skills-by-path`: Refer to other skills and principle files by path instead of pasting excerpts. — reject
- `sections-only-for-non-default-rules`: Include a section only where the person has a specific rule that differs from the default, omitting any section with nothing in it. — reject
- `generic-person-naming`: Say "the user" or "the human" in instructions, never the author's name. — reject
- `vibe-check-evaluation`: Judge a generated working-style skill by asking the person whether it reads like them and what is missing, not by a benchmark loop. — defer
- `persona-scope-excludes-task-skills`: Write task-specific skills and single narrow workflows as ordinary skills without mining, never as a working-style skill. — defer

#### core · Improvement · Codification — skill:pstack/skills/correct
- `recurring-lesson-to-check`: When a correction or instruction recurs, encode it as a lint, flag, runtime check or script instead of adding more instruction text. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `next-agent-test`: Prefer a design where an edit that looks right from one file is right everywhere, assuming the next editor sees only the files it opened and copies the nearest example. — reject
- `mine-and-group-mistakes`: Collect mistakes from recent history, reverts, review remarks, instruction files and workaround comments, and cluster them into classes. — defer
- `two-occurrence-threshold`: Count a class of mistake only after it has happened at least twice. — defer
- `fix-at-highest-level`: Try fixes for a repeated mistake in order of architecture, types, lint or CI, tests and finally docs, stopping at the highest level that works. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#fix-at-highest-level
- `split-ownership-flag`: Give each piece of state one owner, so that others read it or ask the owner to change it, with no second writer and no copy. — reject
- `one-way-per-task`: Keep a single way to do a task, moving callers off the others and deleting them in the same change. — reject
- `unreachable-internals`: Make a module's internals unreachable, so that an import from outside fails the build. — reject
- `derived-or-checked-lists`: Derive duplicate lists from one, or make the build fail when lists that cannot be derived disagree. — reject
- `delete-copyable-old-ways`: Remove outdated approaches and dead code an agent might imitate. — reject
- `unrepresentable-invalid-states`: Shape types so the checker rejects impossible states, defining special cases out of existence instead of handling them. — reject
- `check-error-names-replacement`: Where wrong code can still compile, add a check whose message points at the specific file, type or function to use. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#check-error-names-replacement
- `ratchet-on-common-patterns`: When a pattern is already widespread, fail only on changes that add more of it. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#ratchet-on-common-patterns
- `green-on-break-test-fixed`: Repair or remove a test that stays green when its behaviour breaks. — adopt → principle-test-behavior-not-implementation#green-on-break-test-fixed
- `implementation-test-deletion`: When internals change, rewrite or delete tests that only protect the old implementation, asserting the current contract instead. — reject
- `build-check-over-rule`: Default to building a deterministic check over writing a prose rule for any mechanical finding. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#build-check-over-rule
- `most-frequent-classes-first`: Fix the classes of mistake that occur most often in this pass. — defer
- `small-single-purpose-commits`: Keep each commit small and about one thing. — reject
- `check-proved-on-real-mistake`: Show each new check failing against a mistake that actually occurred. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#check-proved-on-real-mistake
- `same-command-local-and-ci`: Run the identical command on a developer machine and in CI. — defer
- `inline-exception-with-reason`: Record an exception to a check on the offending line along with its justification. — defer
- `expiring-exceptions`: Give every exception to a check an expiry date. — defer
- `human-approved-exceptions`: Require a person's approval for each exception to a check. — defer
- `rule-to-enforcer-table`: Maintain in the agent instruction file a table pairing each rule with what enforces it. — reject
- `correction-adds-rule`: On each operator correction, fix the mistake and also add the rule. — reject
- `unenforced-repeat-escalation`: If a corrected rule already existed without enforcement, count it as a repeat and solve it at the top workable level within that change. — reject
- `structural-fix-only`: Once a rule is enforced by structure, delete the instruction that restated it. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#check-pointer-not-restatement
- `class-evidence-level-report`: Report for every class of mistake the supporting evidence, the chosen level and why no higher level worked. — defer

#### core · Improvement · Codification — skill:pstack/skills/principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
- `recurring-lesson-to-check`: When a correction or instruction recurs, encode it as a lint, flag, runtime check or script instead of adding more instruction text. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `judgement-lesson-example`: When a recurring lesson needs judgement and cannot be checked, make its instruction more prominent and pair it with an example of the failure. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#judgement-lesson-failure-example
- `structural-fix-only`: Once a rule is enforced by structure, delete the instruction that restated it. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#check-pointer-not-restatement

#### core · X · Communication — skill:pstack/skills/bro
- `repitch-trigger`: When a message did not land, stop and re-pitch it rather than adding more. — adopt → brief-me#repitch-trigger
- `controlled-language`: Re-pitch in controlled simplified language with short sentences and common words. — adopt → brief-me#controlled-language

#### core · X · Communication — skill:pstack/skills/ketchup
- `catch-up-window-since-last-message`: Cover what changed since the person's last message, counting notifications and helper results as no message. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#catch-up-window-since-last-message
- `reader-knows-only-their-last-message`: Assume the person recalls their own last message and none of what followed. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#reader-knows-only-their-last-message
- `explain-each-change`: Help the person grasp each change, beyond its current status. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#explain-each-change
- `decidable-from-the-reply`: Set out every waiting decision so the person can make it from the reply alone. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#decidable-from-the-reply
- `catch-up-spoken-register`: Use plain words, short sentences and no jargon, as one person catching another up. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#catch-up-spoken-register
- `outcome-over-method`: Say what changed for the person in their terms, not how it was done. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#outcome-over-method
- `identifiers-only-when-needed`: Omit hashes, paths, commands, build numbers and test counts except where the person needs one to act. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#identifiers-only-when-needed
- `names-the-person-knows`: Call each pull request, branch or agent by a name the person would know, never an invented label. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#names-the-person-knows
- `context-or-omit`: Give a fact the context it needs to make sense, or leave it out. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#context-or-omit
- `catch-up-read-only`: During a catch-up change no code, start no app or job and post nothing, drawing only from material already in hand. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#catch-up-read-only
- `gather-every-source-in-window`: Collect your own work, helper reports and messages from anyone else in the chat since the window began. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#gather-every-source-in-window
- `live-state-of-touched-items`: Check the current state of every pull request, build or agent the chat touched. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#live-state-of-touched-items
- `shown-numbers-verified`: Check each number shown against its source, and say so when one is corrected. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#shown-numbers-verified
- `owner-only-action-items`: Count as an action item only a decision the person alone can take, never work the agent can still do. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#owner-only-action-items
- `pending-calls-carried`: Include every decision still waiting on the person, even one raised before their last message. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#pending-calls-carried
- `no-invented-calls`: Never make up a decision to fill the reply. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#no-invented-calls
- `unrequested-step-excluded`: Leave out a step nobody requested that the work does not need, unless it cannot be undone and waits on the person, which gets one line. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#unrequested-step-excluded
- `calls-group-items`: Let one decision cover many items, such as several pull requests awaiting merge. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#calls-group-items
- `per-item-decision-facts`: Gather for each item its link, its effect on users, the evidence for the pick, its risk and the agent's pick. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#per-item-decision-facts
- `explicit-unknowns`: Write unknown for any needed fact you do not know, and leave out links you do not have. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#explicit-unknowns
- `words-on-decisions`: Spend the words on the decisions, not the story, leaving out work that changed nothing for the person. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#words-on-decisions
- `catch-up-length-budget`: Keep what happened under about a hundred words and each item to about thirty, growing only with the item count. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#catch-up-length-budget
- `never-shrink-items`: Never drop items or replace them with a count or a bare link to meet a length budget. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#never-shrink-items
- `waiting-first-opening`: Open with one sentence naming what waits on the person, or saying nothing does. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#waiting-first-opening
- `nothing-happened-stop`: When nothing happened and nothing waits, say so and stop. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#nothing-happened-stop
- `pictures-first-summary`: Show what happened with pictures first: captured screenshots and videos, then any explanatory diagram. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#pictures-first-summary
- `per-request-outcome-lines`: Give one short line per thing the person requested, with its result and its state: finished, running, failed or unchecked. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#per-request-outcome-lines
- `spoken-sentence-bullets`: Write each bullet as a sentence one would say aloud, not a label and a status. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#spoken-sentence-bullets
- `name-incidental-fixes`: Name any bug found and fixed along the way. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#name-incidental-fixes
- `standalone-true-lines`: Make each line true when read on its own. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#standalone-true-lines
- `no-done-while-waiting`: Never mark done what still waits on the person. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#no-done-while-waiting
- `each-fact-once`: Give each fact once, whether in text, in a picture or in the action items. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#each-fact-once
- `three-takeaways-cap`: Under the summary, add no more than three short lines, each changing what the person knows or has to do. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#three-takeaways-cap
- `remaining-own-work-line`: Say in a single line what work the agent can still do on its own. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#remaining-own-work-line
- `decision-asked-with-pick`: For each action item, ask the decision the person owns and give the agent's pick. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#decision-asked-with-pick
- `pick-names-prereqs-and-irreversibles`: Make the pick cover what the agent would do first, what must come first and what cannot be undone. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#pick-names-prereqs-and-irreversibles
- `cite-item-identifiers`: Give the number or link of each pull request, issue or agent a decision concerns, also inside a choice between options. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#cite-item-identifiers
- `single-item-decision-line`: Put a decision about one item in one line with the decision, pick, user impact, evidence and risk, naming the item once. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#single-item-decision-line
- `shared-decision-riskiest-first`: When items share a decision, state it and the pick once, then one line per item, riskiest first, naming a different pick only for the item that has one. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#shared-decision-riskiest-first
- `always-state-risk`: State every item's risk, low ones included. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#always-state-risk
- `waiting-cost-if-material`: Mention the cost of waiting only when it is worse than a delay, for example a missed deadline or data that would be lost. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#waiting-cost-if-material
- `options-with-gain-and-cost`: For a choice between options, give every option weighed with its gain, its cost and its current state, under its screenshot when one is shown. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#options-with-gain-and-cost
- `figure-when-faster`: Add a figure when a picture would land faster than prose, and omit one for a single simple point. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#figure-when-faster
- `banned-visual-kinds`: Never draw a status list, an action-item list or boxes with no connections. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#banned-visual-kinds
- `glanceable-visual-limits`: Keep each visual to six boxes or fewer with eight words or fewer in each. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#glanceable-visual-limits
- `plain-visual-labels`: Label visuals in plain spoken words, putting any fact that needs a sentence in the text or nowhere. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#plain-visual-labels
- `inline-media-for-visible-changes`: Embed screenshots and videos of a visible change in the reply, not only as links. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#inline-media-for-visible-changes
- `no-screenshot-said`: When a visible change lacks a screenshot, say that it lacks one and describe the change on screen. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#no-screenshot-said
- `diagram-kind-by-content`: Use a diagram for how things connect and a chart for numbers, drawn only from facts in hand. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup#diagram-kind-by-content
- `no-fabrication`: Never fabricate citations, data or examples. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md

- `video-replaces-catch-up-summary`: Run the full catch-up but replace its summary and visuals with a short subtitled video. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#video-replaces-catch-up-summary
- `prior-catch-up-not-a-boundary`: Start a catch-up's window at the person's last message, not at an earlier catch-up. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#prior-catch-up-not-a-boundary

- `render-failure-gives-calls`: If the video fails to render, report that in one line and give only the decisions. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#render-failure-gives-calls
- `slides-from-primary-artifacts`: Build slides from captured screenshots, recordings, diffs and data, not from chat prose about them. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#slides-from-primary-artifacts
- `storyline-before-slides`: Before drawing, write the one sentence the person should take away and one line for each slide, kept out of the reply. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#storyline-before-slides
- `drop-uninformative-slides`: Drop any slide that does not change what the person knows. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#drop-uninformative-slides
- `slide-count-cap`: Use ten slides at most, and fewer by preference. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#slide-count-cap
- `one-point-per-slide`: Make one point per slide. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#one-point-per-slide
- `one-evolving-picture`: Let slides develop one picture rather than cut between unrelated ones. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#one-evolving-picture
- `consistent-visual-encoding`: Keep a colour or shape meaning the same thing on every slide. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#consistent-visual-encoding
- `slides-show-pictures`: Present the work visually, for instance a system's workings, a stack of changes with their states, a before and after, or options side by side. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#slides-show-pictures
- `point-at-the-change`: Direct attention to what changed with arrows, highlights and motion. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#point-at-the-change
- `banned-slide-kinds`: Never make a slide a bullet list, status list, table or set of unconnected boxes. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#banned-slide-kinds
- `labels-on-their-objects`: Keep slide text minimal and put each plain label on the thing it names. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#labels-on-their-objects
- `each-fact-once`: Give each fact once, whether in text, in a picture or in the action items. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#each-fact-once
- `per-request-outcome-lines`: Give one short line per thing the person requested, with its result and its state: finished, running, failed or unchecked. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#per-request-outcome-lines
- `name-incidental-fixes`: Name any bug found and fixed along the way. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#name-incidental-fixes
- `no-screenshot-said`: When a visible change lacks a screenshot, say that it lacks one and describe the change on screen. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#no-screenshot-said
- `no-fabrication`: Never fabricate citations, data or examples. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `one-subtitle-per-slide`: Give each slide one subtitle of about ten words that states its point from what the slide shows. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#one-subtitle-per-slide
- `dedicated-subtitle-strip`: Put subtitles in a fixed strip below the slide that holds nothing else and covers nothing. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#dedicated-subtitle-strip
- `slide-video-format`: Render one silent landscape video whose frames are the slides themselves, with each subtitle burned in for the slide's whole hold. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#slide-video-format
- `reading-time-hold`: Hold each slide at least one second per three newly added words. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#reading-time-hold
- `frame-legibility-check`: Before embedding, look at one frame per slide at chat size to confirm the subtitle reads and covers nothing. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#frame-legibility-check
- `measured-hold-check`: Measure each slide's hold from the file's frames and compare it with the slide's added words. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#measured-hold-check
- `fix-rerender-recheck`: Fix any slide that cannot be read in its hold, render again and check again. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → ketchup-video#fix-rerender-recheck

#### core · X · Communication — skill:pstack/skills/poteto-help
- `how-to-answer-not-run`: Answer a question about how to get something done by explaining it, with a request the person can send and a link to the source, without starting the work. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#how-to-answer-not-run
- `router-at-task-start`: Invoke the router at the start of every task, so routing is loaded on any vendor and comes back after compaction. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `primary-evidence-check`: Check consequential claims from summaries, memory and agent reports against primary evidence before relying on them. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `unclear-need-one-choice-question`: Infer the person's need from context and, only if it stays unclear, ask one multiple-choice question with fixed options and answer only the chosen part. — reject
- `help-setup-state-checks`: Before a help answer, check the setup state that would change it, such as the model configuration, which app-driving and formal verification skills the project has and whether code a formal skill covers changed after its recorded sync, mention each only where it changes the answer, and offer a missing setup at most once per chat. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#help-setup-state-checks
- `onboarding-first-real-task`: Explain getting started as installing, setting up models, then sending a first real task with its goal and a pass-or-fail check. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#onboarding-first-real-task
- `token-cost-guidance`: For a worry about cost, explain where tokens go and which settings cut them. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#token-cost-guidance
- `pack-install-notes`: Explain how the pack installs, persists and is linked on each host, which helper type users may spawn, and which commands come from elsewhere. — out-of-scope
- `host-feature-caveat`: Say which features depend on host abilities, such as spawning helpers, staying loaded across turns or running loops, that another host may lack. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#host-feature-caveat
- `offer-to-word-first-request`: Offer to word the person's first request for them using the prompting guidance. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#offer-to-word-first-request
- `request-states-outcome`: Advise a person to state in a request what is wrong or wanted, a pass-or-fail done check, the proof to show, the evidence they already have and any real constraint. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#request-states-outcome
- `request-omits-method`: Advise a person to say what to achieve and not how, listing no skills or steps except to override one choice. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#request-omits-method
- `withhold-cause-theory`: Advise a person to hold back their theory of the cause until the agent has restated the problem, so it does not narrow the search. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#withhold-cause-theory
- `restate-noisy-report-first`: Before acting on a noisy report, put its underlying problem in plain words so a misreading surfaces before any code is written. — defer
- `ask-for-a-case`: Advise a person to ask the agent to argue for a choice rather than summarize it, since a case is easier to check. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#ask-for-a-case
- `settle-design-in-code-first`: Advise a person to settle an open design question with prototypes of several options, compared on evidence such as screenshots, rather than by reviewing an abstract plan. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#settle-design-in-code-first
- `docs-first-for-shared-api`: For a shared package or interface, write the readme or tutorial first and check the code against it. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#docs-first-for-shared-api
- `plan-after-design`: Advise a person to ask for the plan only once the design settles, with each step ending in a check. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#plan-after-design
- `terse-follow-ups`: Treat a short follow-up such as "do it" or "keep going" as a whole request once the chat holds the task. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#terse-follow-ups
- `new-task-phrase-reset`: Start a fresh playbook pick when a message opens with "new task". — reject
- `away-notice-stops-questions`: Treat a person saying they are stepping away as a signal to stop asking questions. — defer
- `loop-done-as-checks`: Give an unattended loop a done condition written as checks each iteration can run, never a length of time. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#loop-done-as-checks
- `unattended-request-advice`: Advise a person sending unattended work to name a fresh worktree off a base, pre-answer the stops, ask for a decision log and give a stuck exit. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#unattended-request-advice
- `isolate-parallel-writers`: Give parallel agents that would overwrite each other separate worktrees or machines. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#isolate-parallel-writers
- `challenge-green-build-claims`: Advise a person to question a success claimed from a passing build and to ask for proof from the running thing: the command, the user flow, a stored value or a profile. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#challenge-green-build-claims
- `default-to-router`: Recommend the main router by default and name a specific skill only when the person wants more or less than its pick gives. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#default-to-router
- `route-unlisted-by-description`: Route a skill missing from the help table by reading its own description. — reject
- `fixed-confusable-pair-notes`: Keep fixed notes that separate easily confused pairs of skills. — reject
- `steer-by-principle-name`: Steer a drifting run by naming the principle it should apply, which works because the reply names the decision each principle changed. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#steer-by-principle-name
- `steer-by-restating-goal`: Steer a drifting run by restating its goal in one line. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#steer-by-restating-goal
- `short-help-answer`: Lead a help reply with the answer and at most one example request, keeping it short unless the whole map was asked for. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#short-help-answer
- `read-dropped-findings`: Advise a person to read the list of findings an adversarial review dropped, not only those it kept. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#read-dropped-findings
- `read-attention-first`: Advise a person catching up on an overnight decision log to read its attention section first. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#read-attention-first
- `run-failure-troubleshooting`: Answer a run that went wrong from a table that maps common failure symptoms to their fixes. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → mvp-help#run-failure-troubleshooting
- `approve-decision-changing-edits`: Approve only those proposed skill edits that would change a future decision. — reject

#### core · X · Communication — skill:pstack/skills/technical-writing
- `plain-word`: Use the common word over a fancier synonym. — adopt → unslop#plain-word
- `cut-removable-words`: Delete each word a sentence keeps its meaning without. — reject
- `rule-yields-to-better-sentence`: When obeying a writing rule would make a sentence worse, write it another way or leave it as it was. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#rule-yields-to-better-sentence
- `real-name-over-description`: Call a symbol, file, flag or command by its real name instead of a synonym or a description of it. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#real-name-over-description
- `no-coined-terms-unless-defined`: Use the words a developer would say aloud rather than a coined term, keeping a named pattern only where the text explains it at first use. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#no-coined-terms-unless-defined
- `reply-proposes-word-list-changes`: Offer a newly found overused term and its replacement as a proposed change in the reply rather than editing the word list. — reject
- `varied-sentence-lengths`: Vary sentence length on purpose, short for a point and longer for a fact with its condition or consequence. — reject
- `one-thought-per-sentence`: Give each sentence one thought, and each instruction its own sentence, splitting by content rather than length. — reject
- `opinion-where-the-mode-allows`: Take a position on trade-offs in explanation, where opinion belongs, and stay dry everywhere else. — reject
- `name-the-mechanism`: Rewrite a sentence that conveys an impression so that it states a mechanism or number, cutting it if it cannot become an instruction, fact or figure. — adopt → unslop#name-the-mechanism
- `one-mode-per-document`: Keep each document to one of the four documentation modes, splitting mixed content into linked pages. — reject
- `two-question-mode-test`: Choose a document's mode by asking whether it serves action or understanding and learning or work, at any scale from a page to a sentence. — reject
- `tutorial-author-owns-success`: In a tutorial, hold the author, not the learner, responsible for the learner getting through. — reject
- `tutorial-opens-with-what-gets-built`: Open a tutorial by naming the thing the learner ends up with, rather than the skills they gain. — reject
- `tutorial-early-visible-results`: Make each tutorial step produce something the learner can see, early and often. — reject
- `tutorial-says-what-to-expect`: Tell the learner what they should see after a step, such as output, a prompt change or a log line. — reject
- `tutorial-one-clause-explanations`: Cut explanation inside a tutorial to one clause and a link. — reject
- `tutorial-first-person-plural`: Write a tutorial concretely, in the first person plural and as commands. — reject
- `howto-framed-by-problem`: Frame a how-to guide around the problem a person has, not an operation of the machine. — reject
- `howto-action-only`: Assume a competent reader in a how-to guide and link out teaching, background and completeness. — reject
- `howto-branches-allowed`: Allow conditional branches and judgement calls in how-to steps. — reject
- `howto-title-names-task`: Title a how-to guide by the task, not the subject. — reject
- `reference-describes-only`: Keep reference material to description, with no instruction, persuasion or opinion. — reject
- `reference-complete-and-dry`: State every fact, option, limit and error in reference completely, plainly and without hedging. — reject
- `reference-mirrors-the-code`: Shape reference to follow the structure of what it describes, so code and docs are read side by side. — reject
- `reference-where-expected`: Put reference material where readers will look for it. — reject
- `reference-generated-from-code`: Generate reference from the code wherever that is possible. — reject
- `explanation-one-bounded-topic`: Keep an explanation to one bounded topic that reads away from the product, checked by whether its title takes an implied About. — reject
- `explanation-answers-a-why`: Anchor an explanation on a real why question. — reject
- `explanation-gives-background`: Give design decisions, history, constraints and alternatives in an explanation. — reject
- `second-person-present`: Speak to the reader directly as you, in present tense. — reject
- `future-tense-for-later-only`: Use will only for what really happens later. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#future-tense-for-later-only
- `active-voice`: Name the actor in place of a passive, keeping passive only when the actor is unknown or does not matter. — adopt → unslop#active-voice
- `instructions-as-commands`: Write an instruction as a direct command, never as narration or a passive requirement such as should be done. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#instructions-as-commands
- `condition-before-step`: Put the condition, goal or warning ahead of the step it governs. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#condition-before-step
- `common-case-first`: Lead with the common case and follow with its exceptions. — reject
- `plain-expert-register`: Write like a knowledgeable colleague explaining, without buzzwords or figurative language. — reject
- `no-please-in-instructions`: Leave please out of instructions. — reject
- `no-minimizing-words`: Never call a step simple, easy or quick in a procedure. — reject
- `no-announced-future-support`: Do not announce support that does not exist yet. — reject
- `varied-sentence-openers`: Do not start consecutive sentences with the same phrase. — reject
- `descriptive-link-text`: Word a link by its destination's title or content, never as click here. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#descriptive-link-text
- `context-over-outbound-link`: Give a sentence of explanation on the page rather than sending the reader elsewhere with a link. — reject
- `headings-state-the-point`: Make a heading state its section's point rather than only its topic. — reject
- `sentence-case-headings`: Write headings in sentence case. — adopt → unslop#sentence-case-headings
- `heading-grammar-by-type`: Title a task heading with a bare verb phrase and a concept heading with a noun phrase. — reject
- `heading-level-discipline`: Use one top-level heading per page and skip no heading level. — reject
- `numbered-only-for-sequences`: Number a list only when its order matters, and bullet every other list. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#numbered-only-for-sequences
- `list-introduced-by-sentence`: Introduce each list with a complete sentence. — reject
- `parallel-list-items`: Keep the items of a list grammatically parallel. — reject
- `code-and-ui-formatting`: Set code in code font and interface elements in bold. — reject
- `serial-commas`: Put a comma before the last item of a series. — reject
- `partial-list-said-up-front`: Drop etc. and say before a list that it is partial. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#partial-list-said-up-front
- `sentence-word-ceilings`: Split an instruction over about twenty words and any other sentence over about twenty-five. — reject
- `over-compression-fix`: Restore articles, verbs and whole sentences, and spell out arrows, symbols and abbreviations. — adopt → unslop#over-compression-fix
- `one-meaning-per-word`: Give each word one meaning in a document and keep it. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#one-meaning-per-word
- `synonym-cycling-cut`: Keep one term for one referent instead of rotating through synonyms. — adopt → unslop#synonym-cycling-cut
- `fewer-ing-forms`: Avoid words ending in -ing where another form works. — reject
- `limiter-beside-its-word`: Place a limiting word such as only or not right beside the word it limits. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#limiter-beside-its-word
- `noun-stack-unpacked`: Rewrite a stack of nouns as a phrase that states how they relate. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#noun-stack-unpacked
- `pronoun-one-referent`: Make each pronoun point at one obvious noun, repeating the noun when in doubt, and never let this or which stand for a whole clause. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#pronoun-one-referent
- `repeat-article-in-series`: Repeat the article in a series when two items could read as one. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#repeat-article-in-series
- `explicit-conjunction-grouping`: Show what and or or joins, using paired forms such as both and or if then. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → unslop#explicit-conjunction-grouping
- `periods-not-semicolons`: Use a period where a semicolon would join two clauses. — reject
- `em-dash-to-new-sentence`: Replace each em dash with a new sentence. — reject
- `whole-parentheticals`: Write a parenthetical aside as a grammatically complete piece, or move it into a sentence of its own. — reject
- `no-parenthetical-plurals`: Never form a plural with (s). — reject
- `no-unrelated-cleanup`: Avoid cleanup unrelated to the requested work. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `no-idioms-or-latin-abbreviations`: Leave out idioms, colloquialisms, Latin abbreviations and metaphors. — reject
- `writing-rules-cover-pr-bodies`: Apply the general writing rules, all but those for documentation modes, to pull-request descriptions. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → pr#writing-rules-cover-pr-bodies
- `writing-rules-cover-commit-messages`: Apply the general writing rules, all but those for documentation modes, to commit messages. — reject
- `one-minute-pr-briefing`: Write a pull-request body as a briefing a reviewer reads in under a minute. — reject
- `link-bulk-evidence`: Link bulky evidence, such as full logs and commit lists, from a pull request instead of pasting it into the body. — adopt → pr#link-bulk-evidence
- `product-copy-excluded`: Leave product interface strings to the product's own copy guidelines. — out-of-scope
- `tab-indented-snippets`: Indent code snippets with tabs. — reject
- `real-paths-in-docs`: Write real paths in documentation. — reject
- `count-claims-with-command`: Make any count or file-tree claim hold at the landing commit, and give the command that reproduces it. — reject

#### core · X · Communication — skill:pstack/skills/unslop
- `meaning-and-tone-preserved`: Keep the original sense of a text and fit its intended tone when editing it. — adopt → unslop#meaning-preserved-edit
- `ing-phrase-cut`: Delete tacked-on present-participle phrases that claim significance, or back them with real sources. — adopt → unslop#ing-phrase-cut
- `vague-attribution-cut`: Name the source of any claim credited to unnamed groups, or delete the claim. — adopt → unslop#vague-attribution-cut
- `tell-vocabulary-swap`: Replace a fixed list of overused elevated words with plain ones. — adopt → unslop#tell-vocabulary-swap
- `plain-is-has`: Use is or has in place of grand verbs standing in for them. — adopt → unslop#plain-is-has
- `not-just-but-cut`: Replace the construction that denies one thing to promote another with a direct statement of the point. — adopt → unslop#not-just-but-cut
- `forced-triplet-cut`: List as many items as naturally exist, never forcing a group of three. — adopt → unslop#forced-triplet-cut
- `synonym-cycling-cut`: Keep one term for one referent instead of rotating through synonyms. — adopt → unslop#synonym-cycling-cut
- `false-range-cut`: Replace a from-to construction that has no real scale with a direct list. — adopt → unslop#false-range-cut
- `em-dash-ban`: Ban em dashes and their substitutes, including parentheses, en dashes and hyphens as dashes, leaving only periods and commas to separate thoughts. — adopt → unslop#no-em-dash
- `mid-sentence-colon-cut`: Keep colons for lists and examples, rewriting mid-sentence uses and the comparison framing around them. — adopt → unslop#mid-sentence-colon-cut
- `bold-restraint`: Do not bold every proper noun or acronym. — adopt → unslop#bold-restraint
- `inline-header-list-convert`: Turn bullets whose bold label merely restates the line into prose, keeping a period-ended label followed by new detail. — adopt → unslop#inline-header-list-convert
- `sentence-case-headings`: Write headings in sentence case. — adopt → unslop#sentence-case-headings
- `no-decorative-emoji`: Remove ornamental emoji from headings and bullets. — adopt → unslop#no-decorative-emoji
- `straight-quotes`: Replace typographic quotation marks with straight ones. — adopt → unslop#straight-quotes
- `chatbot-phrase-cut`: Remove assistant pleasantries, offers of further help and excited discovery lines. — adopt → unslop#chatbot-phrase-cut
- `sycophancy-cut`: Remove praise and agreement openers and answer directly. — adopt → unslop#sycophancy-cut
- `filler-phrase-cut`: Shorten wordy stock phrases and delete empty announcements of importance. — adopt → unslop#filler-phrase-cut
- `hedge-stack-trim`: Reduce piled-up qualifiers to a single modal. — adopt → unslop#hedge-stack-trim
- `generic-conclusion-cut`: Replace optimistic sign-offs with specific plans or facts. — adopt → unslop#generic-conclusion-cut
- `metaphor-noun-swap`: Replace a listed set of pseudo-technical figurative nouns with their concrete equivalents. — adopt → unslop#local-metaphor-noun-swap
- `name-the-mechanism`: Rewrite a sentence that conveys an impression so that it states a mechanism or number, cutting it if it cannot become an instruction, fact or figure. — adopt → unslop#name-the-mechanism
- `portable-sentence-cut`: Cut a sentence that would fit another project's docs unchanged. — reject
- `dense-sentence-split`: Split or trim any sentence the reader must reread to parse. — adopt → unslop#dense-sentence-split
- `active-voice`: Name the actor in place of a passive, keeping passive only when the actor is unknown or does not matter. — adopt → unslop#active-voice
- `adverb-cut`: Cut an adverb, using a stronger verb or the measured figure in its place. — adopt → unslop#adverb-cut
- `plain-word`: Use the common word over a fancier synonym. — adopt → unslop#plain-word
- `mannered-prose-cut`: Replace aphorisms, rhetorical fragments, personified code, figurative verbs and stock framing with literal phrasing. — adopt → unslop#mannered-prose-cut
- `over-compression-fix`: Restore articles, verbs and whole sentences, and spell out arrows, symbols and abbreviations. — adopt → unslop#over-compression-fix
- `stable-rule-numbers`: Keep rule numbers as permanent identifiers that other documents can cite, leaving a deleted rule's number unused. — reject
