- `bulk-to-subagents`: Send bulk reading and large outputs to subagents and keep only their summaries in the main thread. — adopt → mvp-mode#delegate-independent-by-default
- `phase-scope-caps`: Cap each phase's scope with file limits and turn budgets, counting the context cost of the mechanisms used. — defer

#### core · X · Continuity — skill:pstack/skills/recall
- `current-state-capsule-goal`: Rebuild recent working context into a compact statement of the present position and what comes next. — adopt → recall#current-state-capsule-goal
- `scoped-reading`: Search narrowly and read only the context the task needs, widening when dependencies or uncertainty call for it and never bulk-reading. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `two-record-context-model`: Treat context as living in both the agent's own chat history and a shared record of tracker, chat, docs, source control and error reports. — adopt → recall#two-record-context-model
- `transcript-location-convention`: Locate past chats in a per-workspace folder of line-per-message files named from the workspace path. — out-of-scope
- `recall-routes-away`: First rule out resuming one known chat, making a durable skill from habits and writing a human-facing work summary, since those are other tasks. — adopt → recall#recall-routes-away
- `skip-mining-with-supplied-state`: If the user already gave paths, branch and the change, use that and do no mining. — adopt → recall#skip-mining-with-supplied-state
- `lock-scope-before-search`: Fix the time window, topic and workspace before any searching, and say the locked scope to the user. — adopt → recall#lock-scope-before-search
- `seven-day-default-window`: Treat recent as a real range with a default of seven days. — adopt → recall#seven-day-default-window
- `active-workspace-only-default`: Default to the current workspace and read another project's chats only when asked. — adopt → recall#active-workspace-only-default
- `no-silent-narrowing`: Never quietly reduce a request for everything into a recent subset. — adopt → recall#no-silent-narrowing
- `cheap-model-fan-out`: Spawn concurrent subagents on a fast, inexpensive model, each covering a slice of the chat history. — reject
- `order-by-real-mtime`: Sort candidates by actual modification time, never by identifier name. — adopt → recall#order-by-real-mtime
- `grep-then-read-matching-regions`: Search for the topic first, then open only chats that match and only the parts of them that bear on it. — adopt → recall#grep-then-read-matching-regions
- `exclude-current-and-noise-chats`: Leave out the current chat along with subagent, evaluation and test chats. — adopt → recall#exclude-current-and-noise-chats
- `uniform-per-chat-schema`: Require from each subagent one block per chat recording topic, goal, decisions, unresolved threads, difficulties, corrections and produced artifacts. — adopt → recall#uniform-per-chat-schema
- `finding-cited-by-source-kind`: Cite chat findings by chat identifier and shared-record findings by pull request, ticket, permalink or error-tracker issue. — adopt → recall#finding-cited-by-source-kind
- `direct-search-for-small-corpus`: With one or two chats, search directly without fanning out. — adopt → recall#direct-search-for-small-corpus
- `bulk-to-subagents`: Send bulk reading and large outputs to subagents and keep only their summaries in the main thread. — reject
- `job-fit-helper-effort`: Choose each helper's thinking depth and speed tier to suit its job. — reject
- `default-shared-record-sweep`: Search the shared record by default when a feature, file, subsystem, area or bug is named, omitting it only for activity recall with no named target. — adopt → recall#default-shared-record-sweep
- `one-investigator-per-source`: Hand a shared-record sweep to existing per-source investigators, one for each source. — adopt → recall#one-helper-per-sizeable-source
- `retarget-investigator-question`: Change the investigators' question from design rationale to current state, failed attempts and ongoing user reports. — adopt → recall#retarget-investigator-question
- `sweep-parallel-to-mining`: Run the shared-record sweep at the same time as chat-history mining. — reject
- `empty-search-is-finding`: Count a search that returned nothing as a result to report, not as work to discard. — adopt → recall#empty-search-is-finding
- `unreachable-data-is-gap`: Report data you could not reach, through a missing tool, denied access, retention or deletion, as a coverage gap and never as a null result. — reject
- `primary-evidence-check`: Check consequential claims from summaries, memory and agent reports against primary evidence before relying on them. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `full-transcript-for-agent-behaviour`: When the answer depends on what an agent actually did, read the complete transcript and not a trimmed local copy. — adopt → recall#full-transcript-for-agent-behaviour
- `brief-grouped-by-thread`: Organize a recall brief by thread and stay on the named topic. — adopt → recall#brief-grouped-by-thread
- `brief-section-order`: Present capsule, thread status, problems and next move in that order, with further detail below or cut. — adopt → recall#brief-section-order
- `capped-capsule-section`: Hold the opening capsule to five bullets at most. — adopt → recall#capped-capsule-section
- `status-tagged-thread-lines`: Give each thread one line with exactly one tag from merged, open pull request, in flight, verified uncommitted, reverted or planned. — adopt → recall#status-tagged-thread-lines-with-abandoned
- `capped-recurring-problems`: List at most five recurring problems, including persistent user symptoms and reverted fixes, so the next try starts from the last failure. — adopt → recall#capped-recurring-problems
- `single-next-move`: End with the one most useful concrete next action. — adopt → recall#single-next-move
- `adjacent-excluded-unless-blocking`: Leave out a neighbouring feature or ticket unless it blocks this one. — adopt → recall#adjacent-excluded-unless-blocking
- `cut-detail-before-threads`: When a recall brief passes a screen, remove detail ahead of removing threads. — adopt → recall#cut-detail-before-threads
- `secret-containment`: Keep secrets and private data out of any destination not authorized to hold them. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `reply-is-the-deliverable`: Return the deliverable itself as the reply, never an account of what was done to produce it. — adopt → recall#reply-is-the-deliverable

#### core · X · Continuity — skill:pstack/skills/show-me-your-work
- `single-tsv-decision-log`: Keep one authoritative decision log as a single TSV file with one single-line row per decision. — adopt → decision-trail#single-tsv-decision-log
- `evidence-pointer-cell`: Make a row's evidence cell a resolvable pointer such as a commit, pull request, file and line or artifact path, never narrative. — adopt → decision-trail#evidence-pointer-cell
- `trail-header-template`: Start a new log from a supplied file holding only the header row. — reject
- `trail-six-columns`: Give every row the fixed columns ts in ISO8601, phase or workstream, the decision in one line, why, evidence, and result as an outcome or state. — adopt → decision-trail#trail-six-columns
- `trail-sample-rows`: Show a sample log in the expected plain style. — reject
- `plain-row-wording`: Write rows the way you would tell a colleague, in concrete words, spelling a guiding principle out in place of citing it as a tag. — adopt → decision-trail#plain-row-wording
- `positional-row-helper`: Append rows through a script that takes the log path and exactly five positional cell values, printing usage and failing on any other count. — adopt → decision-trail#named-cell-row-helper
- `hand-append-caveat`: Allow a row appended by hand, giving cells from generated or user-supplied text the helper's byte-level care. — reject
- `decision-points-only`: Log decision points and checkpoints (a chosen fork, a finished unit with its verification, a pivot or revert with its cause, a surfaced blocker, a fixed gate), never each action or a self-evident step. — adopt → decision-trail#decision-points-only
- `row-per-iteration`: Have a looping run write one row for each iteration. — adopt → decision-trail#row-per-iteration
- `helper-aborts-on-failure`: Have the log helper abort on any command failure, unset variable or pipeline failure. — reject
- `creates-log-parent`: Have the log helper create a missing parent directory. — adopt → decision-trail#creates-log-parent
- `header-on-empty-file`: Have the log helper write the header row when the log is missing or empty. — adopt → decision-trail#locked-single-header
- `append-mode-writes`: Write the header and rows only in append mode, so a false empty-file test costs a stray header and never the rows. — adopt → decision-trail#append-mode-writes
- `automatic-utc-stamp`: Have the log helper stamp each row with the current UTC time so the caller supplies none. — adopt → decision-trail#automatic-utc-stamp
- `cell-whitespace-strip`: Replace tabs, newlines and carriage returns in each cell with spaces. — adopt → decision-trail#cell-whitespace-strip
- `formula-cell-quote`: Prefix a single quote to any cell starting with a character a spreadsheet parses as a formula, so hostile text cannot execute when the log is opened. — adopt → decision-trail#numeric-safe-formula-quote
- `run-boundary`: Count one agent conversation with its later turns and summaries as one run, and a pickup, replacement agent or new chat as a new one. — adopt → decision-trail#run-boundary
- `start-row-triggers`: Have a run adding to a log with rows write a `start` row first, and on returning read the log's tail and write a fresh one if another run's `start` has appeared. — adopt → decision-trail#start-row-triggers
- `start-row-contents`: Have a `start` row name the timestamp range of the rows this run did not write and identify this run in its evidence, using the `start` phase for nothing else. — adopt → decision-trail#start-row-contents
- `local-log-default`: Keep the log as an uncommitted working file at a fixed name in the work directory, or under a hidden audit folder by task slug when several efforts run at once. — adopt → decision-trail#trail-location-rule
- `commit-on-reviewer-need`: Leave the log out of Git unless the work is large enough that a reviewer could not trust the outcome without it. — adopt → decision-trail#proposed-trail-commit
- `append-only-supersede`: Never edit or delete a ledger record; correct or reverse one by appending a record that supersedes it. — adopt → decision-trail#append-only-supersede
- `script-evidence-preference`: Favour evidence generated by committed scripts over hand-made one-off evidence. — adopt → decision-trail#script-evidence-preference
- `end-of-run-audit`: Before handing back, check the log for truthfulness against what happened in the run. — adopt → decision-trail#end-of-run-audit
- `transcript-path-audit`: Audit from this run's transcript in the active workspace's transcript directory, whose location the system prompt gives. — reject
- `no-cross-project-transcript-search`: Never search across project transcript folders during an audit, because that exposes unrelated private conversations. — adopt → decision-trail#no-cross-project-transcript-search
- `audit-own-stretches`: Limit an audit to this run's row stretches, each from one of its `start` rows or the log's first row to the next `start` row of another run. — adopt → decision-trail#audit-own-stretches
- `row-maps-to-real-event`: Check that each audited row corresponds to a decision or action that actually occurred. — adopt → decision-trail#verified-record-row-walk
- `evidence-resolves-check`: Check that each audited row's pointer resolves and supports what the row says. — adopt → decision-trail#evidence-resolves-check
- `unlogged-fork-gap`: Treat a fork, pivot or abandoned path that shaped the work with no row as a gap, and add the row in the audit. — adopt → decision-trail#unlogged-fork-gap
- `audit-supersedes-in-place-of-editing`: Have an audit change no row, even an invented one, and add a row superseding it with what really happened and a pointer that resolves. — adopt → decision-trail#audit-supersedes-in-place-of-editing
- `foreign-row-on-own-evidence`: Supersede a row outside the audited stretches only when this run's own work shows it to be wrong. — adopt → decision-trail#foreign-row-on-own-evidence
- `other-family-trail-review`: Before handing back, have a subagent from a different model family review the run, with no self-review in its place. — adopt → decision-trail#same-family-or-unreviewed
- `trail-and-transcript-review`: Give the reviewer the audit trail and the run's transcript as its inputs. — adopt → decision-trail#evidence-pointer-review
- `attention-scan-not-redo`: Have the trail's reviewer look for what is suboptimal or risky for the user's attention and not repeat the work. — adopt → decision-trail#attention-scan-not-redo
- `job-fit-helper-effort`: Choose each helper's thinking depth and speed tier to suit its job. — reject
- `trail-review-flags`: Have the trail's reviewer flag weak or absent evidence, checks skipped or claimed without proof, choices risky in hindsight, and gaps a casual read would miss. — adopt → decision-trail#trail-review-flags
- `attention-section`: End every reply of a run with a trail in an Attention section, opening with a line naming the reviewer's model and then each flag with its rows or moments, where no flags is allowed and the model name is not optional. — adopt → decision-trail#attention-with-coverage
- `trail-reading-method`: Read a trail from top to bottom, following the evidence pointers and spot-checking. — reject
- `trail-rendering-tips`: Show the log as a table through the forge's TSV view or the `column` command. — reject
- `single-trail-format-owner`: Have other skills needing a trail refer to this one by name and define no trail or columns of their own. — reject

#### core · X · Coordination — skill:pstack/skills/arena
- `phase-todos`: Open a task list with one item per phase before beginning. — reject

- `task-rubric-criteria`: Write three to six concrete, gradeable success criteria specific to this task. — adopt → model-council#task-rubric-criteria
- `rubric-withheld-from-candidates`: Keep the success criteria from the candidates, who see only the task. — adopt → model-council#rubric-withheld-from-candidates
- `role-model-config-line`: Read each spawned role's model from a named line of a shared configuration, falling back to a fixed default and leaving the field unset for an alias. — reject
- `rejected-model-swap`: When a spawn refuses a model, use the default and disclose the swap, then the nearest same-family model if the default is refused too. — reject
- `model-family-prefix-map`: Sort models into families by name prefix. — reject
- `unrunnable-seat-dropped`: Remove a seat no valid model can run, and disclose it. — reject
- `seat-backfill-to-minimum`: When dropped seats leave too few runners, add runners up to a floor on a surviving model or the parent's, and disclose the choice. — reject
- `extra-runners-per-direction`: Add candidates when the work must explore several design directions. — reject
- `same-model-for-generation`: Use one model for every seat when output is limited by generation rather than judgment. — reject
- `job-fit-helper-effort`: Choose each helper's thinking depth and speed tier to suit its job. — reject
- `own-output-location`: Give every candidate or adversary a separate output location, so they share no writable state. — adopt → model-council#own-output-location
- `worktree-or-temp-output`: Prefer a git worktree for each candidate's output, falling back to a per-candidate temporary directory. — reject
- `one-message-fan-out`: Launch every candidate or adversary in one message as background subagents. — reject
- `candidate-brief-fields`: Hand each candidate the task, the shared grounding's path and its own output path. — reject
- `rationale-names-rejected`: Have each candidate deliver, with its artifact, a short rationale naming the alternatives it weighed and what it rejected. — adopt → model-council#rationale-names-rejected
- `dropout-proceeds-noted`: Go on with the remaining candidates or adversaries when one produces nothing, and record the dropout. — adopt → model-council#dropout-proceeds-noted
- `judge-after-candidates`: Start the judge only after every candidate has finished. — reject
- `single-judge`: Use exactly one judge for a comparison of candidates. — reject
- `read-only-judge`: Give the judge read-only access. — adopt → model-council#read-only-judge
- `judge-outside-lead-family`: Never let the judge's model share a family with the coordinating agent's model. — adopt → model-council#judge-other-family-or-stated
- `judge-pool-walk`: Choose the judge by trying a pool's entries outside the parent's family in order, skipping parent aliases, moving to a nearby slug or the next entry on refusal and falling back to a default pool. — reject
- `judge-skip-pick-alone`: When no judge can run, skip it, pick the base alone and say so. — reject
- `family-check-unrun-disclosed`: When the coordinator's own model is unknown, try the judge pool in order and disclose that the family check did not run. — adopt → model-council#judge-other-family-or-stated
- `rubric-given-to-judge`: Give the judge the success criteria to score against. — adopt → model-council#rubric-given-to-judge
- `path-labelled-candidates`: Show the judge each candidate under its path label. — adopt → model-council#path-labelled-candidates
- `judge-criterion-scores`: Have the judge score each candidate on each criterion. — adopt → model-council#judge-criterion-scores
- `judge-recommends-base`: Have the judge recommend a base and justify the recommendation. — adopt → model-council#judge-recommends-base
- `judge-parallel-with-picker`: Run the judge while the picker reads, not before or after. — reject
- `full-read-before-pick`: Read every candidate in full before choosing a base. — adopt → model-council#full-read-before-pick
- `picker-criterion-scores`: Score each candidate on each criterion instead of by overall impression. — adopt → model-council#picker-criterion-scores
- `pick-compared-with-judge`: Compare your scored pick with the judge's, treating the same choice as confirmation. — adopt → model-council#pick-compared-with-judge
- `disagreement-rereads-rationales`: Treat a disagreement with the judge as a sign of bias or an unclear rubric, and read both rationales before deciding. — adopt → model-council#disagreement-rereads-rationales
- `base-chosen-for-extensibility`: Choose the base a later maintainer could extend most easily while keeping invariants intact. — adopt → model-council#base-chosen-for-extensibility
- `near-tie-smaller-surface`: Break a near-tie in favour of the cleaner boundary or the smaller interface. — adopt → model-council#near-tie-smaller-surface
- `loser-graft-pass`: Go through each losing candidate once more for parts worth carrying over. — adopt → model-council#loser-graft-pass
- `sparse-grafts`: Expect only one or two grafts from a losing candidate, not the bulk of it. — adopt → model-council#sparse-grafts
- `hand-folded-grafts`: Rewrite each graft into the base by hand, so the result keeps one coherent design rather than pasted fragments. — adopt → model-council#hand-folded-grafts
- `converged-shape-no-graft`: When candidates reach one shape, record the agreement and ship that shape with no graft. — adopt → model-council#converged-shape-no-graft
- `divergence-reframes`: When candidates differ wildly, treat the frame as too loose, then reframe and rerun instead of blending them. — adopt → model-council#divergence-reframes-once
- `synthesized-artifact-verified`: Verify the merged artifact to the same standard as any other output. — adopt → model-council#graft-change-rerun
- `verify-miss-routes-back`: Send a verification problem back to reframing or to grafting, whichever caused it, and never hide it. — adopt → model-council#verify-miss-returns-once
- `single-synthesized-artifact`: End with one merged artifact rather than a set of alternatives. — adopt → model-council#single-synthesized-artifact
- `synthesis-decision-record`: Record the chosen base candidate with its reason, what was grafted from the rest and why each was rejected. — adopt → model-council#synthesis-decision-record
- `note-judge-status`: Record in the synthesis note the judge's verdict or that the judge was skipped. — adopt → model-council#note-judge-status
- `note-convergence-dropouts`: Record any convergence or dropped candidates in the synthesis note. — adopt → model-council#note-convergence-dropouts
- `note-verification-result`: Record the verification result in the synthesis note. — adopt → model-council#note-verification-result

- `design-contest-on-one-way-doors`: For design choices that cannot be undone, run a design skill that pits alternatives against each other, and skip that for mechanical work or a settled design. — adopt → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `fan-out-across-seams-only`: Decide what runs in parallel, parallelizing only where the work has seams and not over-fanning. — adopt → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md

- `job-fit-helper-effort`: Choose each helper's thinking depth and speed tier to suit its job. — reject

- `irreversible-writes-wait`: Always wait for the person before force-pushing a shared branch, deploying, deleting data or messaging a customer. — reject
- `irreversible-only-confirmation`: Ask for confirmation only before irreversible actions such as force-pushing, deleting production data or sending external messages. — reject
- `away-phrase-keeps-going`: Treat phrases such as "don't stop" or "going to bed" as switching the session to continue without stopping. — defer
- `accuracy-over-agreement`: Put factual accuracy ahead of agreement, pointing out errors and unchecked assumptions in the user's thinking. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `single-house-helper-type`: Spawn every helper inside a playbook step as one designated house helper type. — reject
- `routed-skills-keep-helper-types`: Let a routed skill that sets its own helper types for a diverse review keep them, with no override to the house type. — reject
- `no-playbook-in-delegate`: Inside a delegated task, route only to skills and principles and never start a playbook: the parent runs it, and the brief is its step. — adopt → mvp-mode#no-playbook-in-delegate
- `background-every-dispatch`: Run every helper call in the background, steers and resumes included, so no call holds the turn. — reject
- `writable-helper-mode`: Spawn helpers in a writable mode because the read-only mode removes the tool access they need. — reject
- `pointer-only-subagent-briefs`: Keep subagent communication sparse by passing pointers to the spec, tickets, notes and commits rather than copying their content. — defer
- `role-model-config-line`: Read each spawned role's model from a named line of a shared configuration, falling back to a fixed default and leaving the field unset for an alias. — reject
- `vendor-default-role-models`: Ship fixed default model names per role, one for code roles and one for judgement roles. — reject
- `difficulty-tiered-model-choice`: Send the hardest code changes to the strongest judgement model and trivial mechanical edits to the fast code model. — reject
- `job-fit-helper-effort`: Choose each helper's thinking depth and speed tier to suit its job. — reject
- `verification-on-worker-model`: Always run verification work on the parallel-worker model and speed. — reject
- `effort-change-keeps-family`: Never let an effort or speed adjustment change a role's model family, using the nearest available model of that family when the exact one is missing. — reject
- `rejected-model-swap`: When a spawn refuses a model, use the default and disclose the swap, then the nearest same-family model if the default is refused too. — reject
- `read-worker-output`: Open the diff or artifact a worker produced and hold it to the evidence its brief named, instead of relying on its summary. — reject
- `same-prompt-second-opinion`: Get a second opinion by running the same prompt on a different model and treat their agreement as a strong signal. — reject
- `fresh-helper-per-round`: Give each fix round, follow-up or next queue item to a new helper whose brief merges the first brief, all directives since and the previous helper's report, resuming an old helper only to keep costly state such as its checkout, uncommitted changes or a running process. — reject
- `distrust-interrupted-resume`: Treat a helper resumed after an interrupt as having dropped directives, and start a fresh one instead of trusting its done summary. — reject
- `draft-without-machine-patterns`: Write the reply free of machine-written patterns while drafting, since a later cleanup pass does not remove them. — reject
- `one-thought-sentences`: Write one thought per sentence and end each with a period. — reject
- `no-em-dash`: Use no em dashes, ending the sentence or using a comma or parentheses to separate a thought. — reject
- `mid-sentence-colon-cut`: Keep colons for lists and examples, rewriting mid-sentence uses and the comparison framing around them. — reject
- `brevity-keeps-required-sections`: Never let brevity drop a section the reply contract requires, such as details, trade-offs, choices or open decisions. — reject
- `impact-before-implementation`: In a reply, put who the work serves and how it changes things for them ahead of how it was built, followed by what the next owner inherits. — reject
- `only-seen-artifacts-cited`: Link or cite only artifacts produced or read in this session. — reject
- `evidence-label-per-claim`: Attach to every claim, in the same sentence, its evidence or a measured, inferred or guessed label, treating predictions and unseen causes as guesses. — reject
- `run-checks-yourself`: Run any check you are able to run instead of asking the user to run it. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → doc:AGENTS.md
- `full-pr-url`: Give each pull request link as its full web address in the forge's public form. — reject
- `reply-sections-only-unique`: List in each playbook's reply section only what is unique to it, letting a shared style supply the rest. — reject
- `why-only-comments`: Keep a code comment only for a non-obvious reason the code cannot show. — reject
- `assertion-strings-not-step-comments`: Write verify and test scripts without comments narrating their steps, letting assertion and log strings say what each step checks. — reject
- `comment-rule-on-delegate-diffs`: Apply the comment rule to every file produced, helpers' diffs included. — reject
- `playbook-steps-as-todos`: Copy a playbook's steps into the todo list before any task-specific todos. — adopt → mvp-mode#playbook-steps-as-todos
- `recorded-step-skip`: Keep a playbook step that will not run in the todo list, marked with its reason, instead of dropping it. — adopt → mvp-mode#recorded-step-skip
- `bot-comment-three-way-triage`: Sort each automated review thread into fix, dismiss or ask before acting on it. — defer
- `fix-in-owning-pr-with-sha-reply`: Land a review fix in the lowest pull request of a stack that owns the code, then reply on the thread with the commit and resolve it. — defer
- `dismiss-needs-pattern-and-proof`: Dismiss a review comment only when it fits a recorded low-risk pattern and the current code proves no change is needed, with a short reason before resolving. — defer
- `ask-on-risky-or-doubtful-comment`: Take a novel, severe, security, privacy, data or unclear review comment to the user, and ask whenever in doubt. — defer
- `learned-skip-pattern-ledger`: Record each learned skip pattern with its name, confidence tier, when to skip, when never to, sample signals and source, and promote a candidate only after several confirmed dismissals. — defer
- `seeded-skip-patterns`: Start the skip ledger with a few bounded patterns, such as intended visual changes, exports used later in the stack, temporary duplication, warnings an enforced invariant covers, owner-deferred follow-ups and findings the bot withdrew. — defer
- `never-auto-skip-risk-classes`: Never skip a review finding automatically when it concerns security, privacy, money, data handling, schema, concurrency or cross-system effects, or when a small fix clearly lowers risk. — defer
- `human-dismissal-not-precedent`: Treat a past human dismissal of a security or data-flow comment as that owner's judgement, not a rule for skipping later ones. — defer
- `native-behaviour-findings-default-fix`: Default to fixing a logic finding against code that reimplements behaviour the platform already provides. — defer
- `run-contract-test-before-ruling`: When a reviewer says a test pinning prose no longer matches its document, run that test on the branch tip first and let its result decide. — defer
- `security-dismissal-needs-gate-on-tip`: Dismiss a finding about a missing security check only when the branch tip holds that exact check with tests, ahead of the side effect, covering the principal concerned. — defer
- `keep-deliberately-narrow-errors`: Decline to widen a deliberately narrow error condition into a catch-all when the narrowness separates distinct failures, unless the gap is the same kind, loses data or the retry is safe. — defer
- `plan-lint-cli-contract`: Have the plan lint print usage and exit 2 without a file, print each problem as file, line and message and exit 1, and exit 0 when clean. — reject
- `fence-aware-plan-lint`: Skip front matter and ignore text inside properly opened and closed code fences when linting a plan, with regression tests for indented, longer, nested, tilde and mismatched fences. — reject
- `plan-prose-lint`: Flag long dashes, curly quotes and mid-sentence colons in a plan's prose outside code. — reject
- `plan-reading-guide`: Open a plan with a title, an introduction under ten lines and a reading guide that states the box and evidence conventions and points to the playbooks. — reject
- `program-plan-sections`: Require a program plan to carry an ordered program checklist (arming, owners, pull request mechanics, verdict and merge, boot recipe, a main-branch read, an hourly loop and a status message), pull request sections, a close section and only appendices after it, one of them prototype evidence. — defer
- `per-pr-nine-sub-blocks`: Give each pull request section nine bold sub-blocks in a fixed order, with a dependency that names something, checkboxes in the file, build, result, unit and merge blocks, and verify blocks opening with a fixed sentence. — reject
- `ten-lane-live-verify`: Declare live verification as ten numbered lanes on a named worker model at the branch head, each naming a screenshot and a pass condition. — reject
- `perf-verify-four-boxes`: Give performance verification exactly four boxes in order: metric, probe, baseline and rule. — reject
- `review-gate-shape`: Make a plan's review gate either the word None with no boxes, or boxes that mention a screenshot, a video and the operator. — reject
- `plan-box-count-report`: Print each pull request's total checkbox count and its count per sub-block when linting a plan. — reject
- `pr-watcher-modes`: Watch one pull request, the open stack around it or a frozen queued stack until all merge, with a one-shot status table option. — defer
- `draft-gate-option`: Let an opt-in flag stop a draft from blocking, wait for checks before reporting a draft as blocked, and note that a pull request ready under that flag should stay a draft. — defer
- `watcher-output-contract`: Emit machine-readable events by default with an optional human view, exit 64 on bad arguments with errors on standard error only, and give each blocker kind its own exit code. — defer
- `pr-context-resolution`: Resolve repository and pull request from flags, then the local remote, then the branch's pull request, accepting only canonical forge addresses. — defer
- `stack-discovery`: Rebuild a stack from open pull requests' head and base branches, never treating a fork's head as a parent, and settle a merged or closed one before any other query. — defer
- `complete-forge-reads`: Read checks by a fast path with a paginated fallback and page review threads to the end, dropping resolved ones, so no state is judged from a partial read. — defer
- `strict-forge-response-parsing`: Treat a missing key or an unknown value in a forge response as a retryable error carrying the raw value, never as a default. — defer
- `skip-rollup-while-queued`: Skip the commit-rollup query for a queued pull request whose checks are only pending. — defer
- `unknown-check-state-fails`: Count an unknown or unexpected check state as failed and an unfinished one as pending. — defer
- `forge-refusal-outranks-checks`: Treat a blocked merge with a failing head-commit rollup as failing CI even when every visible check is clean. — defer
- `approval-gate-own-kind`: Classify a check that stands for a human approval as its own kind, never pending or failed, so the watcher never waits on it. — defer
- `earlier-pass-flag`: Record with each CI state whether any earlier commit of the pull request passed. — defer
- `review-bot-tracking`: Tag threads opened by review bots, count their distinct passes, and mark review automation as still running while its check is pending. — defer
- `blocker-priority`: Rank blockers as conflicts, open threads, failing checks, merge gates, then pending checks, scanning each tier across the whole stack first and naming the pull request a wait is really on. — defer
- `ready-needs-positive-proof`: Report ready only with positive proof of a clean merge state, no open threads, clean checks and an open review state, enforced by types that reject a ready verdict without it. — defer
- `query-retry-budget`: Poll at validated intervals, back off exponentially with a cap after a failed query, end after a budget of consecutive failures, and cut every wait to an optional deadline. — defer
- `versioned-event-stream`: Give every event a schema version, sequence number, time, mode, kind and terminal flag, emit the captured queue first, advance at once when the frontier merges, and drop repeated identical waits. — defer
- `merge-queue-frontier-polling`: In a merge queue, sweep every unmerged pull request at intervals and otherwise poll only the lowest, resuming a sweep at a failed read and waiting on the queue whatever upstream checks are pending. — defer
- `human-status-rendering`: Render a table of each pull request's checks, review and merge state with full links, and give each blocker a next action. — defer
- `watcher-test-harness`: Pin the watcher's behaviour with tests against a fake forge reader and an injected clock, and typecheck it strictly. — defer
- `self-installing-launcher`: Install a script's dependencies from a frozen lockfile only when a hash of its manifest changes, check the install, then rerun the original command. — out-of-scope
- `bucketed-worktree-report`: List every non-main worktree read-only with its size, age, merge, dirty, remote, pull request and last-chat columns, a suggested bucket by fixed precedence, largest first. — reject
- `base-ref-fallback-and-fetch`: Judge merge state against a ref given by flag, else the remote default, main or master with a warning, fetching it first and only warning if the fetch fails. — reject
- `portable-shell-date-flags`: Detect the platform's `stat` and `date` flags once at start. — out-of-scope
- `pr-state-as-merge-signal`: Treat a pull request's merged state as the merge signal for squash merges, which ancestor checks miss. — reject
- `tracked-wip-vs-untracked-scratch`: Count tracked edits as work in progress and untracked files alone as disposable scratch. — reject
- `remote-push-state`: Report each worktree branch as detached, pushed, ahead by a count, or with no remote branch. — reject
- `last-chat-from-transcripts`: Date a worktree's last activity from the newest chat transcript naming its exact path, counting four days as recent. — reject

#### core · X · Coordination — skill:pstack/skills/principle-never-block-on-the-human
- `reversible-work-proceeds`: Proceed without asking on reversible work, then present the result and its reasoning so the human can correct it afterwards, leaving product direction to the human. — reject
- `noticed-problem-followup`: Log a problem noticed in passing and fix it in the next round. — reject
- `irreversible-only-confirmation`: Ask for confirmation only before irreversible actions such as force-pushing, deleting production data or sending external messages. — reject

#### core · X · Coordination — skill:pstack/skills/setup-pstack
- `role-model-rule-file`: Write one always-loaded rule file that records a budget line and one model per role, overwritten whole on each run. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → setup-mvp-stack#role-model-rule-file
- `detect-selectable-models`: Take the selectable models from what the helper tool accepts this session, preferring a full models list, and ask the person to paste them when none can be found. — reject
- `confirmed-slugs-only`: Write or use a model name only after confirming it is selectable now, never guessing one or carrying it over from someone else's default. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → setup-mvp-stack#confirmed-slugs-only
- `rerun-keeps-role-choices`: On a rerun, start from the existing budget and role values, keep roles the person customized, and drop and list lines for retired roles. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → setup-mvp-stack#rerun-keeps-role-choices
- `budget-tier-rewrites-effort`: Offer four labelled budgets that set the reasoning effort of every role's model, falling back within the family when that effort is unavailable. — reject
- `show-roles-and-confirm`: Show every role with its model, flag undetected ones, and let the person accept or change roles from the detected models. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → setup-mvp-stack#show-roles-and-confirm
- `panel-list-sets-fan-out`: Let a panel role's value be a list, running one helper per entry. — reject
- `judge-outside-lead-family`: Never let the judge's model share a family with the coordinating agent's model. — reject
- `ordered-judge-pool-no-alias`: Take the judge as the first allowed entry of an ordered list of models, never letting an alias that stands for another model be the judge. — reject
- `swarm-worker-model-role`: Set one model for every parallel worker unless a race assigns models per arm. — out-of-scope
- `vendor-default-role-models`: Ship fixed default model names per role, one for code roles and one for judgement roles. — reject
- `new-sessions-notice`: Tell the person the model rule applies from new sessions on and that rerunning updates it. — reject
- `offer-app-driving-generator`: When a project has no way to drive its real app for proof, offer once to generate one and accept a no. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → setup-mvp-stack#offer-app-driving-generator
- `offer-formal-verification-generator`: When a project has no formal verification of its code, offer once to generate a skill for it and accept a no. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.3 → setup-mvp-stack#offer-formal-verification-generator

#### core · X · Coordination — skill:pstack/skills/swarm
- `phase-todos`: Open a task list with one item per phase before beginning. — reject
- `brief-names-done-evidence`: A brief names what will show the work is finished, and a unit with nothing to name is scoped further or raised with the owner before dispatch. — adopt → delegation#brief-names-done-evidence
- `partition-or-race-shape`: Choose whether workers split the work into slices, race on identical briefs or both. — reject
- `race-selection-rule-first`: Fix how the winner of a race is chosen before any worker starts, and apply that rule when merging. — reject
- `role-model-config-line`: Read each spawned role's model from a named line of a shared configuration, falling back to a fixed default and leaving the field unset for an alias. — reject
- `rejected-model-swap`: When a spawn refuses a model, use the default and disclose the swap, then the nearest same-family model if the default is refused too. — reject
- `race-arms-models-named`: Name each racing worker's model before any starts. — reject
- `job-fit-helper-effort`: Choose each helper's thinking depth and speed tier to suit its job. — reject
- `own-output-location`: Give every candidate or adversary a separate output location, so they share no writable state. — reject
- `exact-commit-briefs`: Name the exact commits in the brief of a worker that verifies or measures them. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → delegation#exact-commit-briefs
- `measurement-method-in-brief`: In the brief of a worker that measures, name the method: how many samples, what one sample is and their order. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → delegation#measurement-method-in-brief
- `worker-records-commits-and-method`: Have a worker record in its result the commits and method it actually used. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → delegation#worker-records-commits-and-method
- `one-message-fan-out`: Launch every candidate or adversary in one message as background subagents. — reject
- `cloud-background-workers`: Run workers as general-purpose background agents in the cloud, and locally only when one needs something on the person's machine. — reject
- `worker-base-branch`: Start a cloud worker from a named pushed branch when it must not start from the default. — reject
- `worker-brief-contents`: Give each worker a brief stating the outcome, owned paths, constraints, acceptance checks and pointers to relevant context. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `pass-issues-blocked-verdict`: Have workers report pass, issues or blocked with evidence. — reject
- `every-provable-defect`: Have a worker reporting issues list every defect it can prove, not only the first. — reject
- `dropout-proceeds-noted`: Go on with the remaining candidates or adversaries when one produces nothing, and record the dropout. — reject
- `finished-results-only`: Merge only results that have finished. — reject
- `unanchored-result-respawned`: Discard a result missing the commits and method its brief named, run that worker once more and record a gap after a second miss. — reject
- `missing-result-not-pass`: In coverage work, require a result for every required slice and count a missing one as a gap, never a pass. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.13.2 → delegation#missing-result-not-pass
- `no-raw-worker-dumps`: Keep raw worker output out of the report. — reject
- `swarm-report-table`: Return one report with a result table, one-line issues, gaps and dropouts, and the race rule when one was used. — reject

#### core · U · Tutoring — skill:pstack/skills/teach
- `inspection-only-authority`: Treat a review or analysis request as authority to inspect and report only, never to change the work. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `what-how-why-account`: Cover what a thing is, how it operates and why it has that design. — adopt → teach#what-how-why-account
- `single-blended-account`: Merge the findings of separate investigations into one continuous explanation, never separate reports. — adopt → teach#single-blended-account
- `lead-with-what-matters`: Open an explanation on its central point and on what matters most to this reader. — adopt → teach#lead-with-what-matters
- `confidence-language-kept`: Keep the tier words and hedges that mark uncertainty when editing a finished answer. — adopt → teach#confidence-language-kept
- `pick-few-takeaways`: Choose a small number of things the person should come away understanding before explaining anything. — adopt → teach#pick-few-takeaways
- `learner-context-from-conversation`: Work out why the person is asking and what they already know from the conversation, not by questioning them. — adopt → teach#learner-context-from-conversation
- `depth-where-asked`: Omit what the person evidently already knows and spend the depth on the area they asked about. — adopt → teach#depth-where-asked
- `orient-then-use-investigation`: Read a body of work only far enough to get oriented, and take the digging from a dedicated investigation rather than redoing it. — adopt → teach#orient-then-use-investigation
- `parallel-investigations-combined`: Run the how and why investigations at the same time and merge what they return. — reject
- `investigation-sized-to-question`: Run both investigations for a subsystem and possibly only one for a small change. — reject
- `narrow-rationale-search`: Keep a slow rationale search narrow by default through the question it is given, so it records what it skipped, widening only when the reasoning is the point. — reject
- `plain-definition-first`: Begin by naming the thing and defining it in general terms, using its common name if one exists. — adopt → teach#plain-definition-first
- `general-tied-to-local-case`: After the general definition, connect it to how this codebase uses the idea. — adopt → teach#general-tied-to-local-case
- `build-up-order`: Proceed from definition to mechanism, then deeper reasons, then edge cases. — adopt → teach#build-up-order
- `problem-and-mechanism-per-part`: For each part, explain the problem it addresses and how it actually operates. — adopt → teach#problem-and-mechanism-per-part
- `walkthrough-of-user-action`: When it helps the idea land, trace what happens step by step as someone performs the action. — adopt → teach#walkthrough-of-user-action
- `no-symbol-inventory`: Do not substitute a list of functions and constants for an explanation. — adopt → teach#no-symbol-inventory
- `no-labels-or-step-words`: Print no stock labels announcing the key idea, and never echo a skill's step wording as headers or phrases. — adopt → teach#no-labels-or-step-words
- `smallest-complete-answer-first`: Give a complete answer of one or two sentences first, then stop, adding layers only when asked and never delivering an unbroken block. — adopt → teach#requested-depth-first-answer
- `offer-depth-follow-lead`: Invite the person to go deeper or change topic, and let them steer. — adopt → teach#offer-depth-follow-lead
- `no-quizzes`: Do not test the person or ask them to repeat the idea back. — reject
- `no-teaching-theatre`: Do not announce pauses, sentences to master, or that a part is hard or important; state it, and actually stop when a pause is wanted. — adopt → teach#no-teaching-theatre
- `one-shot-delivery-mode`: When the caller asks for full delivery, give the whole explanation in one reply and place any offer of more depth at the end. — defer
- `show-the-real-artifact`: Bring up the actual diff, source or debugger when that conveys the point most quickly. — adopt → teach#show-the-real-artifact
- `figure-when-faster`: Add a figure when a picture would land faster than prose, and omit one for a single simple point. — adopt → teach#figure-when-faster
- `incremental-diagram-series`: For three or more moving parts, draw a sequence in which each figure repeats the last and adds exactly one part, and never rely on one complete figure, of whatever kind. — adopt → teach#incremental-diagram-series
- `figure-kind-by-idea`: Choose the figure type by the nature of the idea, using a labelled diagram where the labels carry the meaning. — reject
- `complementary-figures`: Use more than one kind of figure when each shows something the other cannot. — defer
- `generated-image-for-spatial-ideas`: For spatial ideas, actually generate a marker-on-whiteboard image with an image tool, with few short labels, instead of describing the picture. — reject
- `plain-colleague-voice`: Write in plain spoken English as if to a coworker, removing filler and hedging while keeping the piece that makes the idea click. — adopt → teach#plain-colleague-voice
- `mechanism-not-metaphor`: State the actual mechanism, never a metaphor, framing or preview of what comes next. — reject
- `density-exemplar`: Supply a worked sample sentence pair that fixes the wanted information density. — reject
- `sentence-case-prose`: Use normal sentence capitalization in prose. — reject
- `no-em-dash`: Use no em dashes, ending the sentence or using a comma or parentheses to separate a thought. — reject
- `comma-budget`: Favour periods, allow at most two commas per sentence, and break a sentence up when clauses accumulate. — reject
- `synonym-cycling-cut`: Keep one term for one referent instead of rotating through synonyms. — reject
- `no-mirror-or-tidy-closer`: Avoid symmetrical constructions and neat concluding lines. — reject
- `reply-is-the-deliverable`: Return the deliverable itself as the reply, never an account of what was done to produce it. — adopt → teach#reply-is-the-deliverable
- `threads-to-chase`: Include the lines of inquiry worth pursuing further. — adopt → teach#threads-to-chase

- `brief-only-read-only`: Tell helpers to write nothing and change no external state even though their mode permits it. — reject

- `code-anchor-first`: Before searching, fix the files, lines, symbols and last commits with blame and rename-following log. — adopt → why#code-anchor-first
- `pr-discussion-pull`: For each substantive commit, read the pull request body, linked issues, comments and reviews. — adopt → why#pr-discussion-pull
- `investigator-brief-assembly`: Build each investigator prompt from a template, one source playbook, one shared code anchor and the original question. — reject
- `full-coverage-search`: Run the search of every available source by default, even an unpromising one, aiming for a complete coverage map. — reject
- `sources-consulted-line`: List each source searched, empty or skipped, with the reason. — adopt → why#sources-consulted-line
- `evidence-source-discovery`: Enumerate the enabled tools and assign each to one of seven evidence categories by its primary evidence. — reject
- `evidence-category-fanout`: Run one investigator per evidence source, all in parallel, with source control always included. — adopt → why#local-evidence-sources
- `repo-evidence-inventory`: Look through commits, pull request threads, inline markers, decision records, changelogs, ticket ids, tests and co-changed files for a repository's history. — adopt → why#local-evidence-sources
- `pickaxe-history-search`: Search history for commits whose diffs add, remove or match a string or pattern. — adopt → why#pickaxe-history-search
- `source-control-trust-ranking`: Rate repository history as the most trustworthy source because it ties directly to the code. — reject
- `incident-source-playbook`: When the target looks defensive, add a search of incident records, incident-labelled tickets and incident channels around the date it was added. — defer
- `incident-commit-signals`: Read commit messages about incidents, added guards or a revert followed by re-application as strong signals of motive. — adopt → why#local-evidence-sources
- `category-strength-map`: State which shape of motivation each evidence category reveals and when it is strongest. — reject
- `provable-irrelevance-bar`: Skip a source for irrelevance only on proof, since probable irrelevance does not qualify. — reject
- `trivial-target-inline-exception`: Answer a single-commit target directly when its pull request text answers fully, after confirming every other search would be redundant. — reject
- `fresh-synthesizer`: Wait for every finding, then have one agent that did no searching weigh the raw findings and write the only answer. — reject
- `framework-first-reading`: Have the writer read the whole confidence framework before writing. — reject
- `gather-without-concluding`: Collect the evidence in full before concluding, forming no answer and picking no side while gathering. — adopt → why#gather-without-concluding
- `confidence-language-kept`: Keep the tier words and hedges that mark uncertainty when editing a finished answer. — adopt → unslop#confidence-language-kept
- `constraints-before-change`: When a change follows, turn the findings into preserve, change, avoid and risk lists. — adopt → why#constraints-before-change
- `recency-bias-check`: Trace past the latest commit, which is not authoritative, to the earlier decisions behind the current shape. — adopt → why#recency-bias-check
- `confidence-tiers`: Place each claim in one tier by its evidence, Direct when an author's written words state the reason, Supported when several indirect items converge, Inferred when a reasonable reading has no explicit support, and Speculative when other explanations fit equally well, phrasing the first two confidently with citations, Inferred with hedges and its reasoning chain, and Speculative as a guess. — adopt → why#confidence-tiers
- `adjacent-citation-gate`: Use words asserting cause, intent, achieved effect or a group decision only on Direct or Supported claims, with a specific citation beside them. — adopt → why#adjacent-citation-gate
- `tier-tagged-sections`: Lay out an answer with one section per evidence class and an explicit tier tag on each bullet, omitting an empty section. — reject
- `searched-and-unknown`: Report an unknown with exactly what was searched, where and with which terms. — adopt → why#searched-and-unknown
- `epistemic-wording-bans`: Ban words that imply self-evidence or triviality and statements of personal belief. — reject
- `no-retrofitted-rationale`: Do not impose a tidy justification on messy history or presume the author chose correctly and reason backward. — adopt → why#no-retrofitted-rationale
- `consistency-is-not-intent`: Do not read a repeated pattern as a deliberate choice, since it may be copying. — adopt → why#consistency-is-not-intent
- `absence-is-not-evidence`: Do not read a lack of mention as proof that something was not a concern. — adopt → why#absence-is-not-evidence
- `embedded-hypothesis-check`: Treat a guess inside the question as one candidate to test independently, then confirm or refute it with citations. — adopt → why#embedded-hypothesis-check
- `contradiction-shown`: Show conflicting sources side by side with citations, leaving the call to the user. — adopt → why#contradiction-shown
- `human-followup-pointer`: Name who could answer a gap and could not be asked, or say the question can be dropped. — reject
- `pre-delivery-claim-audit`: Before delivery, check each claim for a citation or demote it, and check that its phrasing matches its tier. — reject
- `code-not-intent-evidence`: Never cite code or a diff as proof of its author's intent. — adopt → why#code-not-intent-evidence
- `empty-gaps-suspicion`: Treat an answer that mentions no gaps as a warning sign. — reject
- `assigned-slice-depth`: Give each searching helper one assigned slice to go deep on, telling it that peers cover the rest. — reject
- `exact-quote-evidence`: Prefer a precise quotation with a location checkable in seconds to a paragraph of paraphrase. — reject
- `wide-then-narrow-search`: Begin a search with a broad sweep and focus on specific items only afterward. — reject
- `read-whole-item`: Open each item found in full, thread or history included, because a preview or a lone message can mislead. — adopt → why#full-record-reading
- `unreachable-data-is-gap`: Report data you could not reach, through a missing tool, denied access, retention or deletion, as a coverage gap and never as a null result. — adopt → why#unreachable-data-is-gap
- `stop-on-auth-failure`: When a source's tool cannot authenticate, stop and report the source as unsearchable, inventing no findings. — reject
- `correlation-needs-neighbor-check`: Treat a before-and-after shift as suggestive only until other changes landing in the same window are inspected. — reject
- `interest-is-not-cause`: Treat a metric, a logged event or a chart as showing interest only, pairing it with a commit or pull request citation before claiming cause. — reject
- `template-filler-discount`: Discount generic text in a mandatory rationale or template section and look for specific content. — reject
- `plan-date-staleness`: Compare a ticket's or spec's date with what shipped, since plans predate the implementation and go stale. — reject
- `casual-remark-not-a-decision`: Do not count a flippant remark before a commit as a decision, and look for considered discussion. — reject
- `generated-analysis-is-inference`: Use a tool's generated root-cause analysis as inference only, with the actual events and traces as the primary evidence. — reject
- `in-source-leads-only`: Follow references inside your own source and hand cross-source references on as leads without chasing them. — reject
- `counterfactual-strength-test`: Before rating a finding strong, ask whether it would still appear under a false interpretation and what would look different. — reject
- `ambiguity-left-open`: Report ambiguous evidence as ambiguous and leave an unresolved question unresolved over a confident fill-in. — reject
- `neighbor-evidence-substitution`: Do not offer evidence about a neighbouring feature as though it answers the question asked. — reject
- `evidence-record-template`: Have each investigator report its source, then direct items with location, author, date and relevance, and indirect items with inference chain and alternative readings. — reject
- `history-answer-frame`: Open a history answer by restating the question and orienting a cold reader to the code, and close it with confidence rated by sub-claim. — reject
- `competing-hypotheses-section`: When the record fits several stories, give each its evidence for and against, with no forced winner. — adopt → why#competing-hypotheses-section
- `one-reference-per-shared-source`: Give an item cited more than once a single authoritative reference. — reject
- `warehouse-evidence-inventory`: Look for warehouse evidence in product events, usage and billing events, experiment data, system tables and pipeline lineage. — defer
- `typed-models-over-raw`: Query a warehouse's deduplicated typed models, dropping to raw events only where no model serves. — defer
- `dbt-column-conventions`: Use the dbt model fields directly, the standard `_timestamp`, `_id`, `_auth_id`, `_request_id` and `event_name`, typed `properties_<name>` event properties and pre-extracted `context_` client fields, to save a describe round-trip. — reject
- `poll-running-query`: Poll a long-running query's handle for its result in place of running it again. — reject
- `probe-schema-before-query`: Confirm table and column names with listing and describe statements before querying a warehouse, and never report from an unverified table. — defer
- `schema-drift-check`: Check that a field existed when the target was written, since older data may lack it or hold it only in raw form. — defer
- `refresh-lag-fallback`: For events newer than a model's last refresh, query the raw table and deduplicate by id. — defer
- `timeline-against-ship-date`: Compare when a runtime or usage signal rose, fell, first appeared or stopped, and the releases it touched, with the date the target shipped. — defer
- `constant-origin-signal`: Treat a recorded distribution or monitor threshold that matches a constant in the code as evidence of where the number came from. — defer
- `warehouse-motive-signals`: Read an experiment's exposure counts and decision rows, and the expensive queries behind a migration, as warehouse evidence of motive. — defer
- `warehouse-finding-record`: Record each warehouse finding with its type, table, exact query, window, a compact numeric summary with no raw rows, its ship-date correlation and its strength. — defer
- `telemetry-evidence-inventory`: Look for telemetry evidence in metrics, monitors, dashboards, traces, logs, incidents and notebooks, where a metric's or monitor's existence itself shows concern. — defer
- `owning-service-first`: Find the services that own the target, and their dependencies, before searching telemetry. — defer
- `curated-views-before-raw`: Read the dashboards and monitors covering the target, noting their queries and thresholds, before raw telemetry. — defer
- `span-and-trace-inspection`: Use span statistics and specific traces for questions about timeouts, retries, slow paths and cross-service behaviour. — defer
- `narrow-log-lookups`: Narrow log searches by service, tag, text and a window around the change, aggregating in place of dumping raw logs. — defer
- `telemetry-motive-signals`: Read a dashboard by the target's author, an incident naming the code and a pre-change log pattern the guard would prevent as telemetry evidence of motive. — defer
- `telemetry-finding-record`: Record each telemetry item with its type, name, identifier, owner, dates, the condition or query that bears on the question and the strength of the connection. — defer
- `ticket-search-procedure`: Search an external ticket tracker's issues, comments, status updates, project documents, labels and milestones for business motive. — defer
- `named-record-first`: Fetch the records a seed commit names, with their comments, before searching by keyword. — adopt → why#named-record-first
- `target-derived-search-terms`: Build search terms from the target's feature name or business term, symbols, author, error strings and path, trying several wordings. — adopt → why#target-derived-search-terms
- `ship-window-bound`: Bound a search of a large source to a window around the date the target shipped. — reject
- `record-lineage-walk`: From a record, follow its parent and duplicate links to the item that carries the motive. — adopt → why#record-lineage-walk
- `ticket-motive-signals`: Read a stated business problem, a decision comment, an initiative-named parent, an attached spec and motive-bearing labels as tracker evidence of motive. — reject
- `record-finding-fields`: Record each evidence record with its identity, the exact motive quote and its location, its author, its dates and its linked records. — reject
- `ticket-external-metadata`: Record a ticket's labels, project and link with its finding. — reject
- `document-store-search-procedure`: Search a document store's requirement docs, specs, decision records, meeting notes, postmortems and runbooks with broad keywords for unlinked pages, following backlinks, child pages, meeting-note databases and authors' personal spaces. — defer
- `final-draft-preference`: Among several documents on a topic, use the finalized or most recently updated one. — reject
- `document-motive-signals`: Read a matching problem section, rejected approaches, a postmortem naming the fix, dated decision notes and a filled decision record as evidence of motive. — reject
- `document-external-metadata`: Record a document's URL and its final or draft status with its finding. — reject
- `error-trace-relevance`: Open a full error event to see whether its trace crosses the target and its tags and breadcrumbs match the guarded condition. — defer
- `orient-org-and-project`: When an error tracker's organization and project are unknown, look them up before searching. — reject
- `error-finding-record`: Record each error issue with its id, title, project, seen timestamps, event count with sampling, releases, a verbatim trace excerpt, ship-date correlation, link and author notes. — defer
- `chat-search-procedure`: Search team chat for deliberation by the author's messages around the merge date and by the pull request's link. — defer
- `inspect-chat-tool-schema-first`: Check which chat tool exists, its schema and whether it needs authentication before searching it. — reject

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — skill:pstack/skills/architect
- `stub-body-sketch`: Express the shape as signatures and types with stub bodies, pseudocode for tricky logic and comments stating intent and invariants, so that types and signatures alone reveal the data flow, as one file for a small change and a module map for larger work. — adopt → codebase-design#stub-body-sketch
- `phase-todos`: Open a task list with one item per phase before beginning. — reject
- `grounded-sketch`: Before sketching, build a working model of what the design touches and write its architectural explanation, since naming a file is not grounding, skipping this only for true greenfield work. — adopt → codebase-design#grounded-sketch
- `ownership-change-rationale`: When a design changes who owns what or how layers divide, also investigate why the existing shape exists so that its reason becomes a constraint. — adopt → codebase-design#ownership-change-rationale
- `sketch-by-parallel-runners`: Produce candidates through parallel runners on different models, each in its own workspace and told not to hedge, then pick a base on named design axes. — defer
- `role-model-config-line`: Read each spawned role's model from a named line of a shared configuration, falling back to a fixed default and leaving the field unset for an alias. — reject
- `sketch-required-twice`: Require two or more structurally different whole-shape candidates before synthesis, even when the first looks adequate. — reject
- `design-red-flag-screen`: Screen every candidate shape against a named list of design flaws before choosing it, treating any hit as grounds to revise or reject the shape. — adopt → codebase-design#design-red-flag-screen
- `next-agent-test`: Prefer a design where an edit that looks right from one file is right everywhere, assuming the next editor sees only the files it opened and copies the nearest example. — adopt → codebase-design#next-agent-test
- `depth-as-leverage`: Prefer modules whose manageable interface hides a large amount of useful behaviour. — adopt → codebase-design#depth-as-leverage
- `shallow-module-signs`: Treat callers coordinating several methods for one operation, options exposing internal stages, and an interface that does not spare learning the implementation as signs of a shallow module. — adopt → codebase-design#shallow-module-signs
- `leaked-decision-flag`: Reject a design in which one internal decision appears in several modules, so that changing it needs coordinated edits. — adopt → codebase-design#leaked-decision-flag
- `knowledge-not-phase-modules`: Organise modules around one body of domain knowledge, not around execution phases such as load, validate, transform and save. — reject
- `pass-through-flag`: Remove a method that forwards the same arguments with the same shape, unless it adds policy, adaptation or a distinct abstraction. — adopt → codebase-design#pass-through-flag
- `split-ownership-flag`: Give each piece of state one owner, so that others read it or ask the owner to change it, with no second writer and no copy. — adopt → codebase-design#split-ownership-flag
- `one-way-per-task`: Keep a single way to do a task, moving callers off the others and deleting them in the same change. — adopt → codebase-design#one-way-per-task
- `unreachable-internals`: Make a module's internals unreachable, so that an import from outside fails the build. — adopt → codebase-design#unreachable-internals
- `derived-or-checked-lists`: Derive duplicate lists from one, or make the build fail when lists that cannot be derived disagree. — adopt → codebase-design#derived-or-checked-lists
- `synthesis-decision-record`: Record the chosen base candidate with its reason, what was grafted from the rest and why each was rejected. — reject
- `sketch-opt-in-checkpoint`: Proceed from the sketch without a human stop unless the invoker asks for one. — reject
- `sketch-commit-first`: Commit the agreed sketch separately before implementing it. — reject
- `fill-in-breakage`: Accept scoped, planned breakage while filling in a sketch. — reject
- `pushback-triggers-regrounding`: Treat a human objection to the shape as grounding evidence that forces a return to grounding and sketching before more code. — reject
- `implement-against-sketch`: Build against the sketch as the contract, surfacing any departure and revising the sketch first when the code must diverge. — adopt → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/feature.md
- `scrap-on-repeated-friction`: Discard a sketch when implementation repeatedly shows a pattern that it is wrong, such as recurring workarounds, special-case branches, type escape hatches or repeated deviations, and not on isolated problems. — reject
- `scrap-redesign-procedure`: After scrapping, re-explain what exists, redesign as if the new constraints were known from the start, shrink below the old sketch before growing and rerun the candidates. — reject
- `sketch-rationale`: Ship a one-page rationale with the sketch covering the problem and its constraints, the shape with invariants, validation, non-goals and depth, the tradeoffs accepted, at least one rejected alternative, and open questions phrased as questions. — adopt → codebase-design#sketch-rationale
- `caller-usage-first`: Write callers' usage first and derive the types from it, reconciling any divergence toward the usage. — adopt → codebase-design#caller-usage-first
- `next-step-sentence`: State in one sentence what gets built first from the sketch. — reject
- `dominant-access-shape`: Settle the core types first and trace each dominant access pattern through them before writing the logic. — reject
- `no-later-index-gate`: Treat a structure that answers an access pattern with a map, index or cache to be added later as wrong. — reject
- `concurrent-modification-test`: Before sharing state between actors, ask what a concurrent modification would do, and isolate the state unless the answer is nothing. — reject
- `eliminate-shared-writes`: Before coordinating concurrent writers, give each its own write target (file, key, branch or directory) and merge only where results are read. — reject
- `invariant-enforcement-ranking`: Prefer hard-to-misuse types to runtime checks, and runtime checks to comments, for enforcing an invariant. — reject
- `boundary-validation`: Concentrate validation, narrowing and error handling where data crosses a system boundary such as CLI arguments, configuration, the network or an external API. — reject
- `trust-internal-types`: Inside the system, trust data that a boundary already validated into types and propagate errors instead of re-checking it in every layer. — reject
- `pure-core-thin-shell`: Keep business logic in pure functions free of framework dependencies, leaving a thin mechanical shell that calls them. — reject
- `domain-not-wire-types`: Expose domain concepts across a public surface, never the transport, storage or framework types behind it. — reject
- `single-source-of-truth`: Keep each meaning in one authoritative place so changing it is a one-place edit. — reject
- `repeat-and-crash-question`: Ask what happens when a state change runs twice or crashes halfway, and make the transition idempotent where applicable. — reject
- `call-chain-file-limit`: Flatten the hierarchy when following the flow takes more than three files. — reject
